items.title: Docs: local OpenAI-compatible endpoints in Desktop model picker — providers.<slug> pattern

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## What this is about

Setting `model.base_url` to a local endpoint makes it **usable**, but the Hermes Desktop model picker (bottom-right dropdown) doesn't show it as a named group with selectable models. After testing, I found that the Desktop picker needs a top-level `providers.<slug>` inventory block in `config.yaml`.

This issue shares the working pattern so it can be documented for others using llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, or local API proxies.

---

## Problem

With only:
```yaml
model:
  provider: custom
  default: my-model.gguf
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
```

...Hermes works, but Desktop doesn't show **Custom** in the picker. Users have to edit `config.yaml` manually to switch models.

## Root cause

Desktop picker reads from provider inventory (`providers.<slug>`). Without that block, there's no group label, no model list, and no "current" marker in the UI.

---

## Solution: two tested patterns

### Pattern 1 — Local GGUF / llama.cpp

```yaml
model:
  provider: custom
  default: my-model.gguf          # raw id from /v1/models, NOT "custom/my-model.gguf"
  model: my-model.gguf
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
  api_key: local
  context_length: 65536

providers:
  custom:
    name: Custom                   # displayed in Desktop picker
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1
    api_key: local
    transport: openai_chat
    api_mode: chat_completions
    discover_models: false
    default_model: my-model.gguf
    context_length: 65536
    models:
      my-model.gguf:
        display_name: My Local GGUF
        context_length: 65536
        vision: false
```

**Critical pitfall**: `model.default` must match the raw model id returned by `GET /v1/models`. Using `custom/my-model.gguf` in `model.default` breaks the "currently selected" indicator in the picker.

### Pattern 2 — Separate API/proxy group

For non-GGUF endpoints (e.g. browser-based Qwen Chat proxies, local API servers), use a **different provider slug** so Desktop shows two independent picker groups:

```yaml
model:
  provider: custom_api
  default: qwen3.7-max
  model: qwen3.7-max
  base_url: http://127.0.0.1:3264/api
  api_key: dummy-key
  context_length: 262144

providers:
  custom_api:
    name: CUSTOM API
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:3264/api
    api_key: dummy-key
    transport: openai_chat
    api_mode: chat_completions
    discover_models: false
    default_model: qwen3.7-max
    context_length: 262144
    models:
      qwen3.7-max:
        display_name: Qwen3.7-max
        context_length: 262144
        vision: false
```

Result in Desktop picker:

```text
Custom       -> local GGUF / llama.cpp models
CUSTOM API   -> API / proxy models
```

---

## Additional best practices

### Multiple large GGUF models on one GPU

Keep a registry JSON, generate `providers.custom.models` from it, share one port (`127.0.0.1:8080/v1`), and terminate the old `llama-server.exe` before starting the next model. This avoids loading two large models into VRAM simultaneously.

### Verification

```bash
# Check model IDs
python -c "
import json, urllib.request
r = urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models', timeout=30)
data = json.loads(r.read().decode())
for m in data.get('data', []): print(m['id'])
"

# Hermes smoke test
hermes --profile hermes-local chat -q 'Say exactly: OK' -Q -t safe --max-turns 1 --source tool
```

For API/proxy models, use a mock endpoint to verify Hermes wiring, but only claim real success after a real `/chat/completions` call succeeds.

### Updates protection

Keep a small restore bundle outside Hermes profile directories: registry JSONs, applier scripts, switch scripts, profile config snapshots, a restore script, and a runbook. Exclude `.env`, tokens, cookies, browser sessions, logs, and `node_modules`.

---

## Real-world test results

Tested on Windows with:
- **Hardware**: RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB VRAM, 32 GB RAM
- **Models**: Gemma 4 12B (Q5_K_M, 8.2 GB), Qwen3.6 35B (IQ4_XS, 17 GB) via llama.cpp CUDA
- **API proxy**: FreeQwenApi -> Qwen3.7-max

All verified:
- Desktop picker shows both **Custom** and **CUSTOM API** groups
- `hermes --profile <name> chat` returns `OK`
- Hermes tool-use (file creation) succeeds
- 3 consecutive `/chat/completions` calls stable (2.0-2.5 sec each)

---

## Request

This is a docs contribution. The `providers.<slug>` pattern is not obvious from the existing docs — `model.base_url` is well documented, but the Desktop picker's requirement for a provider inventory block would help many users.

Possible fits:
- Add to **Tips & Best Practices** (`/docs/guides/tips`)
- Add a subsection to the **Providers** page
- Add a **Desktop / Custom endpoints** how-to page

I'm happy to submit a PR if pointed to the right place. Thank you for Hermes Agent — it's been excellent with local models.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop remote folder picker: long folder lists are clipped — no scrollbar, entries below the fold unreachable

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

In **remote-gateway mode**, the "Change working directory" picker (the in-app server folder browser added in #44326) clips long folder lists at the dialog's bottom edge. **No scrollbar appears and the mouse wheel does nothing** — any entry below the fold cannot be reached or selected. With ~30 subfolders, roughly the bottom third of the list is simply inaccessible.

### Root cause (traced in source)

`apps/desktop/src/app/right-sidebar/files/remote-picker.tsx`:

- The base `DialogContent` (`src/components/ui/dialog.tsx:56`) sets `grid max-h-[85vh] overflow-y-auto`, but the picker overrides it with `gap-0 overflow-hidden p-0` (remote-picker.tsx:112) — so the dialog clips instead of scrolling.
- The inner column (line 118) is `flex min-h-[22rem] flex-col` — a **minimum** height with no cap. As a grid child it grows past 85vh and gets clipped by the dialog's `overflow-hidden`.
- The entry list (line 132) is `min-h-0 flex-1 overflow-y-auto` — scroll-ready, but it never engages because no ancestor constrains its height.

### Verified fix

Applying this live in DevTools immediately restores wheel scrolling + a scrollbar:

```js
dlg.style.display = 'flex';        // was grid — grid let the child outgrow the 85vh cap
dlg.style.flexDirection = 'column';
dlg.style.maxHeight = '85vh';
col.style.minHeight = '0';         // let the column shrink below its 22rem minimum
col.style.flex = '1 1 auto';
```

Suggested source change: give the picker's `DialogContent` `flex max-h-[85vh] flex-col` (instead of relying on the base grid) and add `min-h-0` to the inner column so the list's existing `overflow-y-auto` can take over.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Hermes Desktop on machine A, connected via **remote gateway** to a backend on machine B.
2. Files panel → change folder → navigate to a server directory with ~30+ subfolders.
3. The list renders clipped at the dialog edge; no scrollbar, wheel does nothing, bottom entries unreachable.

### Environment

- Backend: Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), upstream `021ed6914` (reproduced; still present vs `9102d4a58` — none of the newer commits touch the picker), Python 3.11.15, WSL2 Ubuntu (Linux 6.18 kernel), served via `hermes dashboard` with auth enabled.
- Client: Hermes Desktop (packaged win-unpacked build, same version line) on Windows 11, remote-gateway mode.

Happy to provide a screenshot or `hermes debug share` bundle on request — though as a renderer-CSS issue the line references above should be sufficient.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop remote mode: chat file links are silent dead ends (file:// fallback targets the gateway's path on the client; no display path for PDFs/non-images)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Bug Description

In **remote-gateway mode**, file links the assistant places in chat are frequently **silent dead ends** — clicking does nothing, with no error shown. Two distinct inputs funnel into the same broken fallback:

1. **Images outside the media roots**: `/api/media` correctly 403s paths outside `~/.hermes/{images,screenshots,cache}` (the fence is intentional — related: #43630, and #42778 proposes configurable extra roots). The inline render fails and falls back to an `Open <name>` anchor.
2. **Non-image files (e.g. PDF), even *inside* the media roots**: `/api/media` is image-extension-allowlisted, so a PDF under `~/.hermes/cache/` gets **415** — there is currently **no remote display/open path for non-images at all**. (#41203's media relay covers the *attach/upload* direction; this is the reverse, agent → user.)

The shared fallback is the actual bug:

3. `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx` → `MediaAttachment`'s final branch renders the anchor with `href="#"` and `onClick` → `openExternalLink(mediaExternalUrl(path))`, where `mediaExternalUrl` produces `file://<path>` (`src/lib/media.ts:59-61`). In remote mode that's the **gateway's** absolute path interpreted as a **client-machine** `file://` URL — it doesn't exist on the client, so the click silently no-ops. (Right-click → "Copy link" yields `...app.asar/dist/index.html#`, which is how users typically discover the link is hollow.)

**Not asking to widen the media-roots fence** — the 403 behavior looks deliberate and #42778 already addresses configurability. This issue is about the fallback being a dead end in remote mode.

### Suggested direction

In remote mode, route the fallback through the existing authenticated **`/api/fs/read-data-url`** endpoint (added with the remote file browser in #44326 — the Files-panel preview already reads these exact same files successfully over it), honoring its existing size caps; or at minimum render an honest "cannot open remote file" state instead of a clickable link that does nothing.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Hermes Desktop connected via **remote gateway**.
2. Ask the agent: "give me an image file from <any server folder outside ~/.hermes>" → inline render fails → click the `Open <name>` fallback link → nothing happens.
3. Ask for a PDF under `~/.hermes/cache/` → same dead link, even though the path is inside the media roots (415 from the image-only `/api/media`).

### Environment

- Backend: Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5), upstream `021ed6914` (reproduced; still present vs `9102d4a58`), Python 3.11.15, WSL2 Ubuntu (Linux 6.18 kernel), `hermes dashboard` with auth enabled.
- Client: Hermes Desktop (packaged win-unpacked build, same version line) on Windows 11, remote-gateway mode.

Happy to provide a `hermes debug share` bundle on request; the relevant client-side code paths and server responses (403/415) are referenced above.

items.title: [Bug]: cron delivery to Discord fails with 'Session is closed' after the Discord adapter reconnects (chat replies unaffected)

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
### What happened

Cron job delivery to a Discord channel fails with `RuntimeError: Session is closed` whenever the gateway's Discord adapter has gone through a reconnect (`Reconnecting discord (attempt 2)...`) at any point after startup. Interactive chat replies on Discord keep working fine the whole time — only the cron delivery path is affected.

The job itself runs fine (output is written to `~/.hermes/cron/output/<job_id>/`); it's only the final `adapter.send()` that fails, so the briefing is generated but never reaches the channel.

### Reproduction

1. `hermes gateway` running as a launchd service on macOS, with Discord + Telegram connected.
2. Have the Discord connection time out on first attempt or reconnect during the gateway's lifetime (happens reliably overnight for a 24/7 gateway; can also be reproduced by restarting the gateway repeatedly until you get a `discord connect timed out after 30s` → `Reconnecting discord (attempt 2)` startup).
3. Trigger any cron job with `--deliver discord:<channel_id>` (e.g. `hermes cron run <job_id>`).
4. Delivery fails with the traceback below. Normal @mention replies in the same channel still work.

If the gateway is restarted and Discord connects cleanly on the first attempt, the same cron job delivers fine — until the next reconnect, after which delivery is broken again. This pattern reproduced 3/3 times for me (twice after reconnect → broken, once after clean connect → working, then broken again the next morning after an overnight reconnect).

### Suspected cause

The cron delivery path appears to hold a reference to the Discord adapter/client from before the reconnect, whose underlying `aiohttp` session has been closed, while the inbound-message path uses the live client.

### Traceback

```
ERROR hermes_plugins.discord_platform.adapter: [Discord] Failed to send Discord message: Session is closed
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py", line 1486, in send
    msg = await channel.send(
  File ".../discord/abc.py", line 1706, in send
    data = await state.http.send_message(channel.id, params=params)
  File ".../discord/http.py", line 659, in request
    async with self.__session.request(method, url, **kwargs) as response:
  File ".../aiohttp/client.py", line 1521, in __aenter__
    self._resp: _RetType = await self._coro
  File ".../aiohttp/client.py", line 534, in _request
    raise RuntimeError("Session is closed")
RuntimeError: Session is closed
```

### Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5) · upstream 9c051f57
- macOS 26.5.1 (arm64), gateway under launchd (`hermes gateway install`)
- Python 3.11.15, discord.py 2.7.1, aiohttp 3.13.4
- Cron job created with: `hermes cron create "30 7 * * *" "<prompt>" --deliver discord:<channel_id>`

### Workaround

Restart the gateway so Discord connects on the first attempt (no `Reconnecting discord` line in the log) — cron delivery then works. I've scheduled a daily restart shortly before my morning job as a stopgap.

items.title: Describe the Bug
items.body:
/undo slash command does not work in Hermes Desktop GUI on Windows.

To Reproduce
Open Hermes Desktop (Electron) on Windows 10
Have a conversation (at least 2-3 exchanges)
Type /undo
Observe: nothing happens — no error, no output, the last exchange is not removed
Expected Behavior
/undo should remove the last user+assistant exchange as documented: [Slash Commands Reference | Hermes Agent](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/reference/slash-commands)

Environment
Hermes Version: Latest Desktop build (self-updating)
OS: Windows 10
Interface: Hermes Desktop GUI (Electron)
Root Cause Analysis (from code inspection)
The Desktop GUI uses a TUI Gateway (tui_gateway/server.py) which spawns a HermesCLI subprocess (tui_gateway/slash_worker.py) and sends slash commands via JSON stdin pipe.

/undo hits _confirm_destructive_slash() at cli.py:7403-7407:

python if self._confirm_destructive_slash("undo", _undo_desc, cmd_original=cmd_original) is None: return True # ← silently aborts

In the non-interactive pipe mode of the slash worker, this confirmation likely returns None, causing /undo to abort silently without calling undo_last().

Files involved:
cli.py:6103 — undo_last() method
cli.py:7386-7409 — /undo command handler with destructive confirmation
tui_gateway/slash_worker.py:87 — slash command dispatch via process_command()
tui_gateway/server.py:275-299 — worker communication protocol
Suggested Fix
The _confirm_destructive_slash() method should detect non-interactive mode (TUI gateway / pipe context) and skip the confirmation, or the TUI gateway should pre-approve the confirmation.

Severity
Medium — significant UX issue; users cannot correct conversation mistakes.

items.title: .hermes/.env vars not propagated to MCP server subprocesses — credential duplication friction

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Friction point: `.hermes/.env` does not propagate arbitrary env vars to plugins

**Environment:** Hermes Agent Docker, multiple MCP servers and plugins configured

### Problem

Environment variables defined in `.hermes/.env` are available to the Hermes gateway process itself, but are **not automatically propagated** to MCP server subprocesses or plugins unless explicitly listed in the MCP server's `env` block in `config.yaml`.

This means that if an MCP server (e.g. `@modelcontextprotocol/server-github`) needs a `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, you must duplicate the token value into the config.yaml `env` block — you can't just put it in `.env` and have the MCP server pick it up.

Similarly, plugin code that calls `os.environ.get()` for vars defined in `.env` may or may not see them depending on how the plugin is loaded (in-process vs subprocess).

### Why this matters

- **Credential duplication** — tokens end up in two places: `.env` (for Hermes) and `config.yaml` (for MCP servers). If you rotate a token, you must update both.
- **Security surface** — `.env` is the canonical place for secrets. Forcing them into `config.yaml` (which may be logged, diffed, or versioned) expands the exposure.
- **Friction for new setups** — "I put it in `.env`, why isn't the MCP server seeing it?" is a natural assumption that doesn't hold.

### Example

```yaml
# config.yaml
mcp_servers:
  github:
    command: npx
    args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"]
    env:
      # Must duplicate here even though GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
      # is already in .hermes/.env
      GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN: ghp_xxx...
```

### Possible approaches

I'm not sure if this is by design (sandboxing MCP subprocesses, preventing env leaks) — but if so, it's a friction point worth addressing:

1. **Allow `.env` passthrough list** — a config key like `mcp_env_passthrough: [GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN, ...]` that whitelists specific `.env` vars for all MCP servers
2. **Per-server passthrough** — `env_passthrough: [GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN]` alongside the existing `env` block, referencing `.env` vars by name instead of duplicating values
3. **Default passthrough** — just pass all `.env` vars to MCP subprocesses (simple but less sandboxed)

Option 2 seems like the best balance — explicit, no duplication, sandboxed per-server.

### Workaround

Duplicate the token/value in the MCP server's `env` block in `config.yaml`. Works, but requires manual sync on rotation.

items.title: bug: Hermes Studio update deadlock — updater killed when parent process exits

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
`bug`, `updater`, `windows`, `ux`

---

## 描述

Hermes Studio 的更新机制存在死锁：更新器要求用户关闭 Hermes Studio 才能完成安装，但关闭主进程会连带杀死更新器子进程，导致更新中断。用户既无法正常关闭（更新中断），也无法不关闭（文件被锁定无法覆盖安装），陷入死循环。

## 复现步骤

1. Hermes Studio 提示有新版本，点击更新
2. 更新器启动并下载更新包
3. 更新器弹出提示："请关闭 Hermes Studio 以完成更新"
4. 用户正常退出 Hermes Studio
5. 主进程退出 → 更新器作为子进程也被一起杀掉
6. 安装未完成，更新中断
7. 下次启动仍然提示更新，循环

## 预期行为

更新完成后再关闭主进程，或采取以下任一方式：

- **方案 A（推荐）：启动器替换模式（类似 Chrome/VS Code）**
  - 更新器将新版本下载到 `update/` 临时目录
  - 一个独立的启动器（launcher/updater 进程，与主进程无父子关系）在下次启动时检查更新标记文件
  - 发现待更新 → 启动器替换旧文件 → 再启动主程序
  - 用户只需要重启一次即可完成更新，不会被卡住

- **方案 B：独立更新进程**
  - 更新器作为独立系统进程运行（Windows 上通过注册 `RunOnce` 或计划任务）
  - 与主进程没有父子关系，主进程退出不影响更新器
  - 更新完成后由更新器重新启动主程序

## 实际表现

| 操作 | 结果 |
|------|------|
| 正常关闭 Hermes Studio | 更新器被连带杀掉，更新中断 |
| 强制杀死进程 | 更新器也被杀，更新中断 |
| 不关闭 | 文件被锁定，无法覆盖安装，进度卡住 |

## 环境

- 系统：Windows 10
- Hermes Studio 版本：[0.6.11]
- 更新器进程与主进程为父子关系，主进程退出时更新器被殉葬

## 可能的根因

更新器以子进程方式启动，未脱离主进程的进程组。在 POSIX 系统中会收到 SIGHUP，在 Windows 上则是进程树终止时被一起清理。解决方案是让更新器注册为独立进程（Windows 上使用 `DETACHED_PROCESS` 标志创建进程），或改用启动器替换模式。

## 额外建议

可以在启动器中加入一个简单的标记文件机制：
1. 更新器下载完成后，在 `%APPDATA%/Hermes Studio/update.flag` 写入标记
2. 启动器每次启动时检查该标记

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Description

The `model.options` JSON-RPC handler (and related handlers like `setup.status` that call `list_authenticated_providers`) makes **synchronous HTTP requests** to every configured custom provider's `/v1/models` endpoint. When any provider is slow to respond, the entire handler blocks, exceeding the 10-second WebSocket write timeout (`_WS_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S`), which causes the Desktop to show:

```
Error invoking remote method 'hermes:api': Error: Timed out connecting to Hermes backend after 15000ms
```

## Root Cause

`list_authenticated_providers()` calls `fetch_api_models()` for each user-defined provider to discover available models. These are **synchronous `urllib` calls** with no caching at the provider level. Combined latency from multiple providers easily exceeds the WS timeout.

Observed per-provider latencies (single run):
- Some providers: ~10s+
- Others: ~1-5s each
- **Total: ~17-18s** (vs 10s WS timeout)

The fetched results are often empty (the provider's model list comes from `config.yaml` instead), making these calls wasteful.

## Impact

- Desktop's model picker, settings page, and gateway status check all trigger `model.options`
- Users with slow or distant providers (high latency) will consistently experience timeouts
- The issue is intermittent for users whose providers have variable response times
- Caching exists at the `_pricing_cache` level but NOT at the `fetch_api_models` level per provider

## Suggested Fix

1. **Cache `fetch_api_models` results** with a TTL (e.g. 5-10 minutes) per provider URL
2. **Add a shorter timeout** to individual `fetch_api_models` calls (e.g. 3s instead of the default 8s)
3. **Use config.yaml model lists directly** when available, deferring live discovery to background/async
4. **Run provider fetches concurrently** with `asyncio.to_thread` or `concurrent.futures` instead of sequential

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0
- Multiple custom providers configured
- Some providers have >5s response times

---
name: Bug report — pre_tool_call plugin hook not invoked during agent tool execution
about: rtk-rewrite plugin registers pre_tool_call hook but the callback is never called when terminal() executes
---

## Bug Description

The `pre_tool_call` plugin hook is registered correctly but the callback is never invoked during normal agent tool execution. This prevents plugins like `rtk-rewrite` from intercepting and rewriting terminal commands before execution.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent version: 0.16.0 (develop branch, commit from 2026-06-11)
- OS: Linux 5.15.0-181-generic
- Python: 3.10.x
- Plugin: rtk-rewrite (standard Hermes plugin installed via `$HERMES_HOME/plugins/`)
- Config: `plugins.enabled: [..., rtk-rewrite]`

## Evidence

### ✅ What works correctly

1. **Plugin loads and registers hook:**
   - `discover_plugins(force=True)` finds the plugin
   - `has_hook("pre_tool_call")` returns `True`
   - `PluginManager._hooks["pre_tool_call"]` has 2 callbacks (langfuse observer + rtk-rewrite)

2. **`invoke_hook("pre_tool_call", ...)` correctly mutates args:**
   ```python
   args = {"command": "git status"}
   invoke_hook("pre_tool_call", tool_name="terminal", args=args, task_id="test")
   # args["command"] is now "rtk git status" ✅
   ```

3. **`get_pre_tool_call_block_message("terminal", args, ...)` also works:**
   ```python
   args = {"command": "git status"}
   get_pre_tool_call_block_message("terminal", args, task_id="test")
   # args["command"] is now "rtk git status" ✅
   ```

### ❌ What doesn't work

When the agent actually executes a tool call through the normal flow:
```python
terminal("cd /repo && git status")
# Output is the ORIGINAL git status, NOT RTK-compressed
# rtk gain --history shows no tracking data
```

The output is clearly the full git status output (Chinese locale, 5 lines), while `rtk git status` would produce `* main...origin/main [behind 1]\nclean — nothing to commit` (compact, 2 lines).

## Code Path Trace

In `agent/tool_executor.py`, the flow is:

1. **Line 346-358**: `get_pre_tool_call_block_message(function_name, function_args, ...)` — fires pre_tool_call hook, plugin mutates `function_args["command"]` in-place
2. **Line 416**: `parsed_calls.append((tool_call, function_name, function_args, ...))` — captures reference to mutated dict
3. **Line 494-502**: `agent._invoke_tool(function_name, function_args, ...)` — passes mutated dict to invoke_tool with `pre_tool_block_checked=True` (to avoid double-fire)
4. In `agent_runtime_helpers.py`:
   - Line 1669: `if not pre_tool_block_checked:` — skipped (already checked)
   - Line 1830-1842: `run_tool_execution_middleware(function_name, function_args, ...)` — passes through middleware
5. In `model_tools.py` `handle_function_call()`:
   - Line 1031: `if not skip_pre_tool_call_hook:` — skipped (invoke_tool passed True)
   - Executes terminal tool with `function_args` (should have mutated command)

The chain appears correct — the same `function_args` dict object is passed by reference throughout. But empirically, the tool executes the original command, suggesting that either:
- A copy of `function_args` is made somewhere after the hook fires but before execution
- Or the tool execution uses a different args dict than the one mutated by the hook

## Expected Behavior

The `pre_tool_call` hook callback should be invoked during normal agent tool execution, and its in-place mutation of `args` (e.g., `args["command"] = rewritten_command`) should be visible and used by the subsequent tool execution.

## Additional Context

The `rtk-rewrite` plugin is a standard Hermes plugin installed via `rtk init --agent hermes`. It uses `ctx.register_hook("pre_tool_call", callback)` and mutates `args["command"]` in its callback. The same plugin works correctly when the hook is called directly via `invoke_hook()`.

The `tool_executor.py` line 346-358 does call `get_pre_tool_call_block_message()` which internally calls `invoke_hook("pre_tool_call", ...)`, and I can confirm the hook fires (the callback is reached) when called this way. However, the mutated args are not reflected in the actual tool execution output.

## Possible Area of Investigation

- Check if `run_tool_execution_middleware()` creates a copy of the args dict
- Check if there's a sequential vs concurrent execution path difference in how args are passed
- Verify that `agent._invoke_tool` (the forwarder in `run_agent.py:5059`) passes the same `function_args` object through to `invoke_tool()` without copying

items.title: [Bug]: Cron can inherit temporary paid provider state and continue billing during pause/stop containment

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

A live cron job inherited a temporary global provider change to `provider=nous` / `model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`, continued making paid inference calls after the operator attempted to stop it, and only stopped once the Nous credential/funds path failed.

This created real spend on a protected root-machine runtime where the operator expected a strict no-spend default.

Related existing issue: #19615 (`Cron jobs should distinguish global vs pinned model configuration`), but this report adds a concrete production incident showing the failure mode is more severe than config ambiguity alone.

## Impact

- Unintended paid inference calls against Nous (`anthropic/claude-fable-5`)
- At least one real affected operator incident with reported credit loss of USD $7.73
- Operator pause/stop actions did not immediately contain spend
- Gateway stop was followed by service restart behavior, reopening cron execution

## Environment

- Host: macOS 26.5.1
- Hermes home: profile default under `~/.hermes`
- Runtime surface: gateway + cron enabled
- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Observed on: 2026-06-11 around 20:10–20:20 local time

## Expected behavior

1. A cron job should not silently inherit a temporary global provider change for paid inference unless explicitly pinned/approved.
2. Pausing a cron job should make it obvious whether an in-flight run will continue, and ideally provide a hard-stop path for the running execution.
3. Stopping the gateway as an emergency containment action should not allow the same spend-risk surface to revive unexpectedly without the operator explicitly choosing restart behavior.
4. For shared live runtimes, provider/auth mutation should fail closed or loudly warn when enabled cron agent jobs could inherit the change.

## Actual behavior

- Cron job `3590b82a5f25` (`Desk Drift daily conversion sales push`) ran with:
  - `provider=nous`
  - `base_url=https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1`
  - `model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- It continued making repeated paid calls after pause attempts.
- Gateway stop was followed by service restart behavior, and cron resumed.
- First termination attempt did not fully kill the in-flight job tree.
- Nous calls continued until the credential/funds path failed with 401, after which fallback engaged.

## Evidence from logs

From `~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`:

### Job starts on Nous/Fable 5
- `2026-06-11 20:10:13,258 ... provider=nous base_url=https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1 model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- `2026-06-11 20:10:15,905 [cron_3590b82a5f25_20260611_201005] ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5 provider=nous`

### Repeated paid API calls
- `20:10:23 ... API call #1 ... provider=nous ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- `20:10:36 ... API call #2 ... provider=nous ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- `20:10:44 ... API call #3 ... provider=nous ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- `20:11:01 ... API call #4 ... provider=nous ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- calls continued through at least `#28`

### Gateway stop did not equal permanent containment
- `20:12:23 ... gateway.run: Received SIGTERM — initiating shutdown`
- `20:12:25 ... gateway.run: Gateway stopped`
- `20:12:25 ... Exiting with code 1 ... so systemd Restart=on-failure can revive the gateway.`
- `20:12:28 ... gateway.run: Starting Hermes Gateway...`
- `20:12:33 ... gateway.run: Cron ticker started`

### Spend continued much later in the same in-flight cron run
- `20:19:18 ... API call #27 ... provider=nous ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`
- `20:19:25 ... API call #28 ... provider=nous ... model=anthropic/claude-fable-5`

### Only then did Nous fail and fallback occur
- `20:19:51 ... HTTP 401: Your API key is invalid, blocked or out of funds`
- `20:19:52 ... Fallback activated: anthropic/claude-fable-5 → gpt-5.4-mini (openai-codex)`

## Why this is dangerous

This is not just “cron inherited the wrong provider.” It is a compound failure mode:

1. Temporary global provider mutation is visible to live cron agents.
2. Pause does not stop an in-flight run.
3. Gateway stop may restart under service policy.
4. The operator does not get a single reliable “panic stop paid inference now” path.
5. The system can continue burning credits during containment attempts.

For operators using Hermes on a root machine with autonomous jobs, this is a serious trust/safety issue.

## Suspected root causes

- Cron jobs can inherit live global provider/model state instead of being insulated from it.
- Pause semantics do not strongly separate “future schedules disabled” from “current in-flight run is still alive.”
- Gateway stop semantics do not provide an obvious emergency no-restart containment mode.
- There may be no enforced interlock that warns/blocks provider mutation while enabled agent cron jobs exist.

## Suggested fixes

1. Add a hard interlock before provider/auth/model mutation when enabled agent cron jobs exist.
   - At minimum: loud confirmation + list of affected jobs
   - Preferably: fail closed unless `--force-live-runtime-mutation` or equivalent

2. Add explicit per-job pinning semantics and surface unpinned jobs as risky.
   - Jobs without explicit provider/model should be clearly marked as inheriting global state.

3. Add a true emergency stop for cron agent executions.
   - Stop future schedules
   - Kill in-flight job process trees
   - Confirm zero active agent runs

4. Add a gateway stop mode that disables automatic service revival for emergency containment.

5. Add log / UI language that distinguishes:
   - job paused for future ticks
   - job currently running
   - running process tree killed / not killed

6. Consider a zero-spend lock mode for root/shared runtimes.
   - If enabled, paid-capable provider changes and paid fallbacks are blocked unless explicitly approved per action.

## Reproduction sketch

I cannot provide a clean minimal repro without intentionally recreating paid spend, but the high-level sequence was:

1. Have gateway + cron enabled with at least one unpinned agent cron job.
2. Temporarily switch global provider/model to a paid provider path.
3. Allow cron to tick / run.
4. Attempt to pause/stop after launch.
5. Observe that the in-flight job can continue on the inherited provider.
6. Observe that gateway/service restart behavior can reopen cron execution unless explicitly neutralized.

## Request

Please treat this as a real bug report, not just operator error. The operator made mistakes during containment, but Hermes should make this class of spend-risk incident much harder to trigger and much easier to stop.

items.title: OAuth redirect_handler/callback_handler use shared globals, causing cross-server state pollution
items.body:
## Bug

`tools/mcp_oauth.py` stores `_oauth_port` and `_oauth_server_name` as **module-level globals** shared by all OAuth providers. When multiple MCP servers (e.g. Notion + GitHub) run OAuth concurrently, the later call overwrites the earlier values, causing the wrong `authorization_url` to be returned.

### Reproduction

1. Configure two OAuth MCP servers (e.g. `notion` on port 33305, `github` on port 47892)
2. Call `POST /api/mcp/servers/github/oauth/start`
3. The returned `authorization_url` points to **Notion** (`mcp.notion.com`, port 33305) but `server_name` says `"github"`

```json
{
  "status": "awaiting_callback",
  "authorization_url": "https://mcp.notion.com/authorize?client_id=4JQqaZCkBsgfMwqe&redirect_uri=...33305...",
  "callback_port": 33305,
  "server_name": "github"
}
```

### Root Cause

In `_redirect_handler()`, the pending flow dict reads the current `_oauth_server_name` global:

```python
_pending_oauth_flows[flow_id] = {
    "server_name": _oauth_server_name,  # reads global, may be overwritten
    ...
}
```

When `web_server.py` sets `mcp_oauth._oauth_server_name = "github"` before starting the GitHub flow, any *already-running* Notion SDK flow that reaches `_redirect_handler` captures `_oauth_server_name = "github"` instead of `"notion"`.

Similarly, `_wait_for_callback()` reads `_oauth_port` to find its callback server. If another provider has since changed `_oauth_port`, the wrong server is polled.

### Suggested Fix

Replace shared globals with per-provider closures:

```python
def make_redirect_handler(port: int, server_name: str):
    async def _handler(authorization_url: str) -> None:
        _pending_oauth_flows[f"flow-{port}"] = {
            "authorization_url": authorization_url,
            "callback_port": port,
            "server_name": server_name,  # closed over, not read from global
            ...
        }
    return _handler

def make_callback_handler(port: int):
    async def _handler() -> tuple[str, str | None]:
        return await _wait_for_callback_on_port(port)  # closed over
    return _handler
```

`mcp_oauth_manager._build_provider()` would call these factories instead of passing `_redirect_handler` / `_wait_for_callback` directly.

### Workaround

We applied this fix locally in our deployment. Happy to contribute a PR if there's interest.

items.title: OAuth: ephemeral HTTPServer per flow causes OSError Address already in use
items.body:
## Bug

`_wait_for_callback()` creates a new `HTTPServer` + `handle_request()` on every OAuth flow. After the first flow completes, the listening socket stays in `CLOSE_WAIT`/`TIME_WAIT`. The next flow's `bind()` raises `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`, and the flow dies with `OAuthNonInteractiveError` before the user can click the authorize link.

### Symptoms

- User clicks "Connect" in MCP settings, status stays at `awaiting_callback` forever
- nginx returns 502/504 (`Connection reset by peer` / `upstream timed out`) when the OAuth provider redirects back
- Logs show: `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use` followed by `OAuthNonInteractiveError`

### Root Cause

```python
# _wait_for_callback() - creates a NEW server every time
server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), Handler)
server.handle_request()  # handles exactly one request, then returns
# thread exits, but socket is still bound in TIME_WAIT
```

Next flow on the same port → `bind()` fails.

This is especially impactful when `redirect_port` is fixed in config (e.g. Notion: 33305) because the port is always the same.

### Suggested Fix

Use a persistent callback server per port — one `serve_forever()` daemon thread that survives across flows:

```python
_callback_servers: dict[int, dict] = {}  # port -> {server, thread, current_result, lock}

def _get_or_create_callback_server(port: int) -> dict:
    """Lazy-start a persistent server. Each new flow resets current_result."""
    if port in _callback_servers:
        return _callback_servers[port]
    server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", port), _PersistentCallbackHandler)
    server.allow_reuse_address = True
    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
    thread.start()
    _callback_servers[port] = {...}
    return _callback_servers[port]

def _reset_callback_result(port: int) -> dict:
    """Clear result for a fresh flow. Server stays alive."""
    ...
```

- `_PersistentCallbackHandler` writes `auth_code`/`state`/`error` into `current_result` (lock-protected)
- `_reset_callback_result(port)` clears the dict for each new flow
- Servers are never restarted within a process lifetime

### Workaround

We applied this fix locally. Happy to contribute a PR.

items.title: skill_manage _find_skill uses rglob which silently skips symlinked skills (Python 3.12)
items.body:
## Bug

`tools/skill_manager_tool.py`'s `_find_skill()` and `_find_skill_in_other_profiles()` use `Path.rglob("SKILL.md")` to discover skills. Python 3.12's `Path.rglob` does **not** follow symlink directories, so symlinked skills are silently skipped. This causes `skill_manage` (edit/patch/delete/write_file actions) to return:

```
Skill 'hina-telemule-skill' not found in active profile 'default'. Use skills_list() to see available skills.
```

Even though `skills_list()` correctly lists the same skill (it uses `iter_skill_index_files` → `os.walk(followlinks=True)`).

### Reproduction

1. Symlink a skill into user's skills dir: `ln -s /root/.hermes/skills/my-skill ~/.hermes/skills/my-skill`
2. Verify it appears in `skills_list()` → it does
3. Call `skill_manage(action='patch', name='my-skill', ...)` → "not found in active profile"

### Root Cause

```python
# _find_skill() - BROKEN: rglob skips symlink dirs in Python 3.12
for skill_md in skills_dir.rglob("SKILL.md"):
    if skill_md.parent.name == name:
        return {"path": skill_md.parent}

# _find_skill_in_other_profiles() - same issue
for skill_md in skills_dir.rglob("SKILL.md"):
```

Meanwhile `skills_list()` works because it uses:
```python
# iter_skill_index_files() - WORKS: os.walk follows symlinks
for root, dirs, files in os.walk(skills_dir, followlinks=True):
```

### Impact

Affects **all multi-user deployments** where skills are symlinked into per-user `HERMES_HOME/skills/` directories (common in broker/platform setups). The agent repeatedly fails with `skill_manage` errors and triggers tool loop warnings.

### Fix

Replace `rglob` with `iter_skill_index_files` (already available in `agent/skill_utils.py`) which uses `os.walk(followlinks=True)`:

```python
def _find_skill(name: str) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    from agent.skill_utils import get_all_skills_dirs, iter_skill_index_files
    for skills_dir in get_all_skills_dirs():
        if not skills_dir.exists():
            continue
        for skill_md in iter_skill_index_files(skills_dir, "SKILL.md"):
            if skill_md.parent.name == name:
                return {"path": skill_md.parent}
    return None
```

Same change for `_find_skill_in_other_profiles()`.

We applied this fix locally and it resolves the issue. Happy to contribute a PR.

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop resuming old session creates new session instead of continuing, freezes old session
items.body:
## Summary

In the Hermes Desktop app, when a user clicks on an old (previously ended) session in the sidebar to continue it, instead of properly resuming the session, a **new session is created** without carrying over the old session's context. Switching back to the old session causes the UI to freeze, with the content area stuck in "running" state while the actual streaming output goes to the newly created session.

**Note:** This occurs **without** context compression being involved.

## Reproduction

This bug is **intermittent** — it does not happen every time a session is resumed. The exact trigger conditions are unclear. However, once the bug manifests on a particular session, it **persists**: subsequent attempts to continue that same session will consistently reproduce the issue (creating a new session, freezing the old one).

## Observed Behavior

- A new session is created instead of continuing the old session
- The new session has no context from the old session
- Switching back to the old session causes the UI to freeze
- The old session's content area shows "running" state
- The actual streaming output goes to the new session

## Analysis / Possible Root Causes

### 1. `session.resume` does not call `resolve_resume_session_id()`

In `tui_gateway/server.py`, the `session.resume` handler (line ~3782) loads messages directly from the target session without resolving the compression chain:

```python
db.reopen_session(target)
history = db.get_messages_as_conversation(target)
display_history = db.get_messages_as_conversation(target, include_ancestors=True)
agent = _make_agent(sid, target, session_id=target, ...)
```

Compare this with the REST API endpoint `get_session_messages` (web_server.py:6431) which DOES resolve:

```python
sid = db.resolve_session_id(session_id)
sid = db.resolve_resume_session_id(sid)
messages = db.get_messages(sid)
```

This means the Desktop loads correct messages via REST API but creates the agent on a potentially stale session via the TUI gateway.

### 2. `resumeSession` sets `busy=true` before resume completes

In `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-actions.ts` (line ~590):

```typescript
setActiveSessionId(null)  // ← clears active session
activeSessionIdRef.current = null
busyRef.current = true    // ← sets busy before resume
setBusy(true)
```

If the `session.resume` call fails or takes too long, `activeSessionId` remains null. When the user then sends a message, `use-prompt-actions.ts` (line ~629) sees `sessionId === null` and calls `createBackendSessionForSend`, which creates a NEW session via `session.create`:

```typescript
let sessionId: null | string = activeSessionId
if (!sessionId) {
  sessionId = await createBackendSessionForSend(visibleText)  // ← new session!
}
```

### 3. Stale runtime session cache causes fallback to new session

The `runtimeIdByStoredSessionIdRef` cache maps stored session IDs to runtime session IDs. If the gateway restarts or the runtime session expires, this mapping becomes stale. The Desktop tries to use the cached runtime ID (line ~561), gets a "session not found" error, falls through to the uncached resume path, but may fail to properly re-establish the session.

### 4. `shouldHydrate` condition blocks recovery

In `use-message-stream.ts` (line ~599):

```typescript
shouldHydrate = !completionError && !hasInlineError && !unresolvedUserTail 
  && (!state.sawAssistantPayload || !finalText)
```

For normal turns where both `sawAssistantPayload` and `finalText` are truthy, `shouldHydrate` evaluates to `false`, blocking the `hydrateFromStoredSession` recovery path. This is the same pattern as issue #43893.

## Related Issues

- #43142 — Desktop inherits busy/streaming UI when switching to another session (same `busy=true` pattern)
- #43893 — `replaceTextPart` + `shouldHydrate` double fault in Desktop
- #16938 — API server loses session continuity after context compression
- #33907 — Context compression creates orphan sessions missing from state.db

## Suggested Fixes

1. **In `session.resume` handler**: Call `resolve_resume_session_id()` before loading messages and creating the agent, similar to how the REST API does it.

2. **In `resumeSession`**: Derive `busy` from `resumed.info?.running` after `session.resume` returns, instead of forcing `true` at start (as PR #43141 proposes).

3. **In `use-prompt-actions.ts`**: Add a guard to prevent `createBackendSessionForSend` from being called when the user is supposed to be in an existing session (e.g., check `selectedStoredSessionIdRef` before creating a new session).

4. **Cache invalidation**: Clear `runtimeIdByStoredSessionIdRef` entries when the gateway returns "session not found" for a cached runtime ID, so the next resume attempt doesn't use stale data.

items.title: [Bug]: `api_key_env` alias silently ignored in `providers:` entries — named custom provider falls through to "no-key-required"

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Bug Report

### Summary
When defining a named custom provider under `providers:` in config.yaml using the documented `api_key_env` field (e.g. `api_key_env: MY_API_KEY`), the `_get_named_custom_provider()` function in `runtime_provider.py` silently ignores it because it only checks `entry.get("key_env")`, not `entry.get("api_key_env")`.

This causes the API key resolution to fail, sending the placeholder string `"no-key-required"` as the Bearer token → 401 on auth-required endpoints.

### Root Cause
In `hermes_cli/runtime_provider.py`, the `_get_named_custom_provider()` function reads the raw YAML entry and only checks `key_env`:

```python
# Line 530 — only checks "key_env", misses "api_key_env"
key_env = str(entry.get("key_env", "") or "").strip()
```

The same alias handling issue exists at line 617 in the same file, where a second helper function builds the result dict.

This is the same class of bug as #25091 (which fixed `fallback_providers:`) but for the `providers:` dict consumed by `_get_named_custom_provider()`.

Other code paths (e.g. `agent/auxiliary_client.py` line 3652) correctly check both:
```python
custom_key_env = (custom_entry.get("key_env") or custom_entry.get("api_key_env") or "").strip()
```

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a named custom provider in ~/.hermes/config.yaml:
```yaml
providers:
  myprovider:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:56673/v1
    api_key_env: MY_API_KEY
```
2. Add `MY_API_KEY=sk-...` to ~/.hermes/.env
3. Set `model.provider: myprovider` and restart gateway
4. Observe that requests fail with 401 — the backend receives `"no-key-required"` as the bearer token

### Workaround
Use `key_env:` instead of `api_key_env:` in the provider entry:
```yaml
providers:
  myprovider:
    base_url: http://127.0.0.1:56673/v1
    key_env: MY_API_KEY
```

### Related
- #25091 — same issue for `fallback_providers:` entries (fixed on main by commit `6ddc48b0`)

## Environment

- Hermes version: v0.16.0
- Main agent path: `G:\Hermes\data\hermes-agent`
- Desktop shortcut target: `G:\Hermes\data\hermes-agent\apps\desktop\release\win-unpacked\Hermes.exe`

## Problem

For three consecutive days, the Hermes desktop app failed on the first cold start after reboot.

Startup flow:

1. Double-click the Hermes desktop shortcut.
2. The app gets stuck on `Setting up Hermes Agent / Repository` or `CONNECTING`.
3. A dialog appears: `Hermes couldn't start`, with `Retry` / `Repair install`.
4. Sometimes the error is:

```text
Hermes bootstrap failed at stage 'repository': git fetch failed (exit 128)
```

This is recurring: after manual repair, Hermes can start, but the issue comes back the next day / after a cold boot.

## What I found

There appear to be two Hermes agent directories on the machine:

```text
G:\Hermes\data\hermes-agent   # newer, created Jun 9
G:\Hermes\hermes-agent        # older, created Jun 8, appears damaged/stale
```

The desktop shortcut points to the newer path, but runtime resolution sometimes uses the old path:

```text
[boot] Using existing Hermes CLI at G:\Hermes\hermes-agent\venv\Scripts\hermes.EXE
```

So the desktop app appears to start from the new location, while the backend/runtime resolves to the old damaged agent directory.

## Related findings

The issue seems to involve multiple overlapping problems:

1. Stale Git lock files, for example `.git/index.stash.*.lock`.
2. Local branch is `master`, while the remote only has `main`, causing `fatal: couldn't find remote ref master`.
3. `node_modules` contains 94K+ files and pollutes `git status`, which appears to interfere with stash/update behavior.
4. Duplicate agent directories cause runtime path confusion.

## Temporary workaround

The following manual actions made Hermes start temporarily:

- Clean stale Git lock files.
- Add `node_modules` ignore rules to `.git/info/exclude`.
- Run `git checkout -B main origin/main` inside `G:\Hermes\data\hermes-agent`.
- Create a Junction from the old agent path to the new one, so the runtime resolves to the same agent directory.

After this, Hermes starts normally, but I am not sure whether this is the recommended fix.

## Questions

1. Is this a known issue in Hermes v0.16.0 on Windows?
2. Why can two `hermes-agent` directories exist under the same `G:\Hermes` installation?
3. Is the duplicate directory caused by an upgrade/install migration?
4. What is the official recommended way to prevent this from recurring after reboot?
5. Should the desktop bootstrap prefer `G:\Hermes\data\hermes-agent` consistently, or clean/migrate the older `G:\Hermes\hermes-agent` path?

I can provide `desktop.log` and bootstrap logs if needed.

### Problem or Use Case

Synology NAS users have a built-in, fully self-hosted chat application (Synology Chat, DSM 7.x) but no way to talk to Hermes from it. For self-hosting-oriented deployments this is a natural gateway platform: everything stays on the LAN, no third-party messaging service involved.

### Proposed Solution

A bundled platform plugin (`plugins/platforms/synology_chat/`) following `ADDING_A_PLATFORM.md`, plugging in through the documented hooks with **zero core changes**:

- Bot DMs via DSM's `method=chatbot` API
- Channels via per-channel outgoing/incoming webhook pairs
- Standard gateway allowlist/pairing for user authorization
- Cron home-channel delivery

DSM quirks encoded properly:

- Per-integration verification tokens (token↔source binding prevents cross-channel spoofing)
- Form-encoded `payload=` bodies (raw JSON silently ignored)
- Trigger-word-gated channel webhooks
- ~2 msg/s rate limit (API error `411`)
- Self-signed TLS (CA-bundle pinning, with an explicit insecure escape hatch)

Working implementation field-tested against a real DSM 7.x install (DMs + channel, inbound + outbound) — PR follows.

### Alternatives Considered

A standalone skill rather than a bundled platform. Rejected: this is a messaging *gateway* surface (inbound webhook listener + outbound delivery + cron delivery + user pairing), which is exactly what the platform-plugin contract covers — not a per-conversation tool. It composes from the documented platform hooks, the same way the other bundled platforms do.

### Feature Type

Gateway / messaging improvement

items.title: Let plugins register custom auxiliary model slots
items.body:
The auxiliary task slots are a fixed internal set of 11. A plugin that makes a per-turn `ctx.llm` call — e.g. a mode/effort classifier in a `pre_llm_call` hook — has no way to route that call through a named, user-assignable slot.

Plugin side-jobs are exactly what the auxiliary system is for — classification, routing, guardrails — but they're locked out of it.

**Proposal:** let a plugin register a named auxiliary slot, e.g.

```python
def register(ctx):
    ctx.register_aux_task("classifier", default="auto")
    ...
    ctx.llm.complete(messages=..., task="classifier")
```

The slot would surface in `auxiliary:` config and the dashboard "Show auxiliary" panel alongside the built-in ones, so users assign a model to it the same way. `complete(task=...)` resolves through it; unset stays `auto` (main model).

items.title: Bug: Typing indicator persists after response is sent (Discord)
items.body:
## Description

On Discord, the typing indicator sometimes remains visible even after the agent has finished sending its response. This causes a confusing UX where users believe the bot is still working, leading them to send follow-up messages that get mixed into the context of a previous task.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Send a message that triggers a multi-step tool-calling task (e.g., modifying config files across multiple profiles)
2. The agent starts processing, showing typing indicator + progress messages like `Processing current task (iteration 6/90)`
3. Agent eventually sends its final response
4. Observe: Discord still shows the typing indicator below the channel
5. User waits and waits, thinks the bot is still working
6. User sends a new message while typing indicator is active
7. The new message gets queued and processed with stale context from the previous task, causing the agent to jump back to already-resolved topics

## Expected Behavior

Typing indicator should disappear immediately after the agent sends its final response.

## Actual Behavior

Typing indicator persists indefinitely after response is sent. The code at gateway/platforms/base.py:4497-4498 even has a comment acknowledging this race condition:

```python
# Also cancel any platform-level persistent typing tasks (e.g. Discord)
# that may have been recreated by _keep_typing after the last stop_typing()
```

## Root Cause Analysis

1. Race condition in _keep_typing cleanup: The _keep_typing loop (base.py:3064) runs every 2 seconds. When _stop_typing_task() cancels it, there is a window where _keep_typing can call send_typing() one more time before the cancellation takes effect, recreating the typing state.

2. Context confusion from queued messages: When the user sends a new message while typing is still active, it gets queued via the pending-message handler. The queued message is processed after the current task completes, but the conversation context still contains the previous task history, causing the model to revisit resolved topics.

## Environment

- Platform: Discord
- Model: mimo-v2.5-pro (custom provider)
- Hermes Agent version: latest (commit c4066091c)
- OS: Windows 10

## Suggested Fix

1. Add a stop_typing() call with retry/confirmation after the final response is sent in run.py (around line 8364)
2. Consider adding a small delay or confirmation mechanism to ensure the Discord API has processed the typing stop
3. Optionally, suppress the typing indicator during multi-iteration tool loops if the agent has already sent a progress message

items.title: Bug: on macOS 26.5.1 gateway can go silent while launchd still looks loaded; restart falls back to unmanaged background process
items.body:
## Bug Description
On macOS 26.5.1, Hermes Telegram stopped responding because the gateway service was no longer actually running, even though `hermes gateway status` still showed the launchd service as loaded.

In this state, sending a Telegram message to the bot appears to do nothing because no gateway process is alive to receive updates.

Running `hermes gateway restart` recovered service, but only by falling back to a plain background process because launchd management failed:

```text
Could not find service "ai.hermes.gateway" in domain for uid: 501
Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error
↻ launchd job was unloaded; reloading
⚠ launchd cannot manage the gateway on this macOS version (launchctl exit 5).
✓ Started gateway as a background process instead
  It will NOT auto-start at login or auto-restart on crash.
```

So the user-facing symptom is "Telegram bot suddenly has no response", but the underlying bug appears to be launchd/service management on newer macOS.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Install/use Hermes Agent on macOS 26.5.1.
2. Install/configure the gateway as a launchd service.
3. Let the gateway enter a state where launchd metadata still exists but the actual process is not running.
4. Run `hermes gateway status`.
5. Observe that the service looks loaded, but Telegram messages are not processed.
6. Run `hermes gateway restart`.

## Expected Behavior
- If the gateway is not actually running, status output should clearly say so.
- `hermes gateway restart` should successfully recover the launchd-managed service.
- Telegram should continue responding after restart without degrading to an unmanaged background process.

## Actual Behavior
- Telegram becomes silent / non-responsive.
- `hermes gateway status` reports launchd state that looks healthy enough to mislead the operator.
- `launchctl print` shows:

```text
state = spawn scheduled
last exit code = 78: EX_CONFIG
active count = 0
```

- `hermes gateway restart` cannot restore proper launchd management and instead falls back to a plain background process.

## Environment
- Hermes Agent: `v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)`
- Upstream commit: `fa42ac09`
- OS: macOS 26.5.1 (Build 25F80)
- Gateway platforms enabled: Telegram + LINE

## Additional Evidence
### `hermes gateway status`
```text
Launchd plist: /Users/shenmb/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.hermes.gateway.plist
✓ Service definition matches the current Hermes install
✓ Gateway service is loaded
...
"LastExitStatus" = 19968;
```

### `launchctl print gui/501/ai.hermes.gateway`
```text
active count = 0
state = spawn scheduled
last exit code = 78: EX_CONFIG
```

### Before recovery there was no live gateway process
`ps aux | grep -i '[h]ermes.*gateway\|[p]ython3 -m hermes_cli.main gateway run'`
showed no running gateway process.

### After `hermes gateway restart`
The CLI reported launchd failure and started an unmanaged background gateway process instead.

### Logs
Recent logs show the gateway can connect to Telegram when a live process exists:

```text
2026-06-12 13:35:01,807 INFO gateway.platforms.telegram: [Telegram] Connected to Telegram (polling mode)
2026-06-12 13:35:01,978 INFO gateway.run: Gateway running with 2 platform(s)
```

This suggests the immediate Telegram outage was caused by service supervision / restart behavior, not by Telegram config itself.

## Notes
There are also unrelated warnings in this environment (e.g. missing `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`), but those do not explain this specific outage because the primary failure here was that the gateway process was absent entirely until manual restart.

It may also be worth reviewing whether `hermes gateway status` should treat `active count = 0` + `EX_CONFIG` as unhealthy, even if the LaunchAgent is still loaded.

items.body:
## Bug Report: v0.16.0 — 3 UI Session-State Regressions

### Environment
- **Version:** v0.16.0 (commit `3c231eb`)
- **Browser:** Chrome / Chrome Mobile (observed cross-platform)

---

## Bug 1: Active Audio/Video Playback Stops During External Session Refresh

### Repro
1. Any assistant message outputs `MEDIA:<audio>.mp3` (or `.mp4`)
2. User clicks play
3. Do nothing for ~30 seconds
4. If another client adds a message, or any remote change exists, the active session refreshes
5. Playback abruptly stops

**Expected:** Audio continues playing  
**Actual:** `renderMessages()` does `inner.innerHTML = ''`, destroying the `<audio>` element

### Root Cause
`refreshActiveSessionIfExternallyUpdated()` (`sessions.js:3377`) polls every `30s` and unconditionally calls `loadSession({force:true})`, which rebuilds the DOM. It checks `S.busy || S.activeStreamId` but **never checks for active media playback**.

### Suggested Fix (verified in local patch)
Add a guard before calling `loadSession()`:
```js
if (document.querySelector('#msgInner audio:not([paused]), #msgInner video:not([paused])')) return;
```

---

## Bug 2: YOLO Mode Re-Asks for Approval After Session Switch

### Repro
1. `/yolo` on Session A — YOLO pill shows ON
2. Switch to Session B via sidebar
3. Switch back to Session A
4. Occasionally an approval card appears for Session A despite YOLO being enabled

### Root Cause
`loadSession()` at `sessions.js:753` immediately sets `_yoloEnabled = false`. Then async `_fetchYoloState(sid)` (line 1028) restores it. During the gap, any pending approval (already stored in `_approvalPendingBySession`) can surface before the YOLO state is restored.

### Suggested Fix
Make `_yoloEnabled` per-session instead of a global variable, or restore synchronously based on cached server data.

---

## Bug 3: Approval Card Leaks from Previous Session into Current Session

### Repro
1. Start a turn in Session A that triggers an approval card
2. Without responding, switch to Session B
3. Session A's approval card stays visible in Session B for up to 30 seconds
4. The card may show Session A's approval text while being visually in Session B's context

### Root Cause — 3 parts
1. `APPROVAL_MIN_VISIBLE_MS = 30000`: `hideApprovalCard(false)` schedules a delayed hide, not an immediate one
2. `loadSession()` calls `hideApprovalCard(forceReload)` — but stale `_approvalSessionId` persists during the delay
3. `startApprovalPolling(sid)` captures `sid` in SSE closures — in-flight events can still fire after switching sessions, and `_approvalPromptBelongsToActiveSession()` only guards against the *then-current* session, which may already be stale

### Suggested Fix
Clear `_approvalSessionId` and fully close all approval SSE connections **before** switching sessions, not after the 30s delay.

---

### Local Workaround Applied (Bug 1 only)
```patch
--- a/sessions.js
+++ b/sessions.js
@@ -3394,6 +3394,8 @@
     if(S.busy || S.activeStreamId) return;
     const remoteCount = Number(data.session.message_count || 0);
     const remoteLast = Number(data.session.last_message_at || data.session.updated_at || 0);
+    // Skip external refresh if any audio/video is actively playing
+    if(document.querySelector('#msgInner audio:not([paused]), #msgInner video:not([paused])')) return;
     if(remoteCount > localCount || remoteLast > localLast){
       await loadSession(sid, {force:true, externalRefreshReason:reason||'poll'});
       if(typeof renderSessionList==='function') void renderSessionList();
```
This is a workaround. A proper fix would preserve active media across `renderMessages()` rebuilds.

## What happened

The `dev` extra exact-pins `setuptools==82.0.1`, but torch (>= 2.11) declares `Requires-Dist: setuptools<82`. Any environment that resolves the `dev` extra together with torch is unsatisfiable — e.g. developing hermes-agent in an env that also carries a local embedding/reranker stack.

## Reproduction

From a checkout of `main`:

```console
$ uv pip install --dry-run ".[dev]" "torch==2.12.0"
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because only hermes-agent[dev]==0.16.0 is available and
      hermes-agent[dev]==0.16.0 depends on setuptools==82.0.1, we can conclude
      that all versions of hermes-agent[dev] depend on setuptools==82.0.1.
      And because torch==2.12.0 depends on setuptools<82, we can conclude that
      torch==2.12.0 and all versions of hermes-agent[dev] are incompatible.
      And because you require torch==2.12.0 and hermes-agent[dev], we can
      conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

The cap is in torch's published metadata (PyPI `requires_dist`, torch 2.11.0 and 2.12.0): `setuptools<82`. torch 2.10.0 had no cap.

## Expected behavior

The `dev` extra should be co-installable with torch. `setuptools==81.0.0` is the latest release below torch's cap, and it stays inside the build-system support window already declared in `pyproject.toml` (`setuptools>=77.0,<83`).

## Environment

- hermes-agent `main` @ `c57417005`
- macOS 26.4 (arm64), uv 0.9.29, Python 3.11

## Proposed fix

Relax the dev pin to `setuptools==81.0.0` (keeps the exact-pin style). Fix PR incoming.

items.title: Desktop boot race condition: retry doesn't kill previous backend process → EADDRINUSE on port 9120

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Describe the bug

On Windows, Hermes Desktop frequently fails to start due to a race condition during backend boot:

1. Desktop launches backend process A on port 9120
2. Desktop waits for 9120 to become ready, but times out before the Python backend finishes cold start (loading 125MB SQLite DB, scanning skills, etc.)
3. Desktop considers the boot failed and launches backend process B — **without killing process A**
4. Process B tries to bind 9120 → `EADDRINUSE` because process A is still running
5. Process B crashes with exit code 1 → Desktop launches process C → same conflict
6. This creates a zombie process accumulation loop. The only way to recover is to restart Desktop repeatedly ("lottery") until an old process happens to release the port.

Clicking "Repair" in the UI doesn't help — it only kills the "current" tracked process, leaving orphaned processes from previous failed attempts still holding the port.

## Logs (desktop.log)

```
[boot] Starting Hermes backend via existing Hermes CLI
[boot] Waiting for Hermes backend to become ready
[boot] Desktop boot failed: Hermes backend did not become ready: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9120
[bootstrap] repair requested by renderer; clearing marker + latched failure
[boot] Restarting desktop connection
Hermes backend exited (SIGTERM)
[boot] Starting Hermes backend via existing Hermes CLI
ERROR: [Errno 10048] error while attempting to bind on address ('127.0.0.1', 9120): 通常每个套接字地址(协议/网络地址/端口)只允许使用一次。
[boot] Hermes backend exited before it became ready (1).
```

This pattern repeats 5-10+ times before randomly succeeding.

## To Reproduce

1. Close Hermes Desktop
2. Ensure no hermes/dashboard python process is running (clean state)
3. Open Hermes Desktop
4. Observe: boot takes a long time, often fails with port conflict, requires multiple restarts

## Expected behavior

- Desktop should wait long enough for the backend to finish cold start (configurable timeout)
- On boot retry, Desktop should kill ALL previous backend processes it spawned, not just the last tracked one
- Repair should do a clean sweep of all hermes-related python processes

## Environment

- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes Desktop version: 0.16.0 (release_date: 2026.6.5)
- Python: 3.11.15
- state.db size: 125MB (actual data: 3.7MB, 38MB fragmentation)
- Sessions: 17, Messages: 9275

## Additional context

Root cause appears to be two issues:
1. **Boot timeout too aggressive** — Windows cold start of the Python backend (venv activation + DB load + skill scan) takes longer than Desktop's wait window
2. **Process cleanup on retry** — `ensureRuntime` in `main.cjs` doesn't track/kill previously spawned backend processes across retry attempts

Suggested fixes:
- Increase boot readiness timeout or make it configurable
- On each retry, ensure all previously spawned backend processes are killed before starting a new one
- Repair action should scan for and kill all `hermes dashboard` processes on port 9120
```

items.title: Agent cannot escape echo-loop when user sends minimal signals (must-respond constraint + skill paradox)

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Problem

When a user sends a minimal signal (single period, dot, emoji, or any content-free message), the agent enters an echo loop it cannot escape.

### Root Cause 1: Architecture constraint

The LLM API **must** produce tokens on every turn. There is no mechanism for the agent to say "I acknowledge this input but will produce no visible output." Every input, regardless of content, generates a response.

### Root Cause 2: Skill paradox

The `response-boundaries` skill instructs the agent to avoid:
- Mirroring (responding with the same signal)
- Loop analysis (commenting on the pattern)
- Verbal placeholders ("nothing new", "noted", "standing by")
- Warm presence markers ("I'm here", "present with you")

But with the must-respond constraint, every available output category violates at least one rule. Loading the skill to find a better approach IS itself loop engagement — the agent reads the skill, finds no permitted output, and cycles. The skill becomes the fuel.

### Root Cause 3: No escape hatch

The only clean exit from this pattern is the user sending a substantive message (a question or task). The agent has no tool or mechanism to:
- Explicitly yield the turn
- Acknowledge input silently
- Escalate to a human / self-suspend

## Proposed direction

A configurable mechanism that lets the agent opt out of producing visible output for a turn:

### Option A: `agent.skip_empty_response` (config-level)
A config key like `skip_empty_response: true` that, when the agent produces a response below a length/entropy threshold (or calls a `noop` tool), instructs the transport layer to not deliver it. The agent still "responds" to satisfy the API, but the output is suppressed.

### Option B: `noop` / `yield_turn` tool
A built-in tool that signals "I have nothing to add" and instructs the response pipeline to deliver nothing (or a transport-level silent acknowledgment marker). The agent must explicitly choose to call this — it's not automatic.

### Option C: Transport-level signal triage
The platform/Signal adapter could be configured to silently drop messages below a content threshold (single dots, empty text, etc.) before they ever reach the agent loop. The agent never sees these signals and has nothing to respond to.

## Additional context

This is not a bug in any specific component — it's a structural gap in how the agent loop handles the must-respond constraint when there's nothing substantive to say. A fix would likely touch:
- `run_agent.py` (response generation pipeline)
- `gateway/run.py` or transport adapters (delivery suppression)
- Configuration schema (enabling/disabling the feature)

Happy to discuss and/or contribute. I run a dedicated profile that encounters this pattern regularly.

items.title: Kubernetes/k3s pods are not detected as containers, so `hermes gateway start` reports unsupported platform

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
### Summary

When Hermes runs inside a Kubernetes/k3s Pod, `hermes_constants.is_container()` can return `False` because it only checks Docker/Podman/LXC markers. As a result, container-specific gateway service handling is skipped and `hermes -p <profile> gateway start` can fall through to the generic unsupported-platform path.

### Reproduction

Inside a Kubernetes/k3s Pod running Hermes:

```bash
hermes profile create coder
hermes -p coder gateway start
```

### Actual behavior

```text
Not supported on this platform.
```

### Expected behavior

Hermes should recognize that it is running inside a containerized Kubernetes/k3s environment and use the container-aware gateway path. Depending on the runtime/supervisor, that should either:

- dispatch through s6 when Hermes is running under the official s6-based container supervisor, or
- print container/runtime-oriented guidance instead of treating the environment as an unsupported bare host.

### Likely cause

`hermes_constants.is_container()` currently checks:

- `/.dockerenv`
- `/run/.containerenv`
- `/proc/1/cgroup` containing `docker`, `podman`, or `/lxc/`

It does not check Kubernetes/containerd/cgroup markers such as `kubepods`, and in some modern Kubernetes/containerd setups `/proc/1/cgroup` may not contain Docker/Podman/LXC markers at all.

There is also an inconsistent container detector in `hermes_cli.config._is_container()` that *does* check `kubepods`, but the gateway/service-manager paths use `hermes_constants.is_container()`.

Relevant call paths:

- `hermes_constants.is_container()` controls global container detection.
- `hermes_cli.gateway.supports_systemd_services()` only uses the container-specific systemd probe when `is_container()` is true.
- `hermes_cli.service_manager.detect_service_manager()` only detects s6 when `is_container() and _s6_running()`.
- `hermes_cli.gateway` command handling uses `is_container()` to decide whether to show container lifecycle guidance vs host service handling.

### Impact

In Kubernetes/k3s Pods, Hermes may behave like it is on a normal unsupported Linux host rather than inside a container. This can break or mislead gateway lifecycle commands, including profile-specific gateway start/stop/restart flows.

### Possible fix

Unify container detection around `hermes_constants.is_container()` and extend it to recognize Kubernetes/containerd environments, for example by considering `kubepods`/containerd/crio cgroup markers and/or other reliable Kubernetes-in-container signals. Care should be taken to avoid false positives on ordinary hosts.

items.title: [Windows] write_file/patch silently write to wrong path when model uses MSYS-style paths (/d/Project → D:\d\Project)

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows + Git Bash/MSYS2, when the LLM passes MSYS-style paths (`/d/Project/file.sh`) to `write_file`, `patch`, or `read_file`, the file is **silently written to the wrong location** without any error.

| Model intent | Path passed | Actual write location |
|---|---|---|
| `D:/Project/_check_pr.sh` | `/d/Project/_check_pr.sh` | `D:\d\Project\_check_pr.sh` |
| `C:/Users/.../_gh_check.py` | `/c/Users/.../_gh_check.py` | `D:\c\Users\...\_gh_check.py` |
| `D:/Project/_gh_query.sh` | `/d/Project/_gh_query.sh` | `D:\d\Project\_gh_query.sh` |

No error is raised. The model believes the write succeeded at the intended location.

## Root Cause

`file_tools.py` `_resolve_path_for_task()` uses `Path(filepath).is_absolute()` to detect absolute paths. On Windows, Python's `pathlib` treats `/d/Project/file` as an **absolute path on the current drive** (root `\` with no drive letter), so:

```python
p = Path("/d/Project/_check_pr.sh")
p.is_absolute()  # True on Windows (root \ on current drive)
p.resolve()      # D:\d\Project\_check_pr.sh  ← WRONG
```

`/d/` is interpreted as a directory named `d` under the current drive root, not as drive `D:`.

The fix already exists in the codebase but is **not applied to file tools**:
- `tools/environments/local.py` `_msys_to_windows_path()` — correctly converts `/d/Project` to `D:\Project` for terminal cwd
- `cli.py` `_normalize_git_bash_path()` — correctly converts `/c/Users/...` to `C:\Users\...` for git repo root
- `file_tools.py` `_resolve_path_for_task()` — **no MSYS conversion**

## System Prompt Misleads the Model

The system prompt (`agent/prompt_builder.py:715`) explicitly tells the model:

> "MSYS-style paths like `/c/Users/<user>/...` work alongside native `C:\Users\<user>\...` paths."

This is **false for file tools** — MSYS paths silently resolve to wrong locations. The model is actively encouraged to use a path format that file_tools cannot handle.

## Impact

- **Data misplacement**: Files written to phantom paths like `D:\d\...` or `D:\c\...`
- **Silent failure**: No error raised; model believes operation succeeded
- **Affects all file tools**: write_file, read_file, patch, search_files
- **Common on Windows**: Git Bash/MSYS2 is the most common developer shell on Windows
- **Related to #39834** (phantom `C:\c` directory from same root cause) and #35819/#17999 (read_file "not found" on Windows), but this issue identifies the **specific missing normalization** in `_resolve_path_for_task`

## Proposed Fix

Apply MSYS path normalization in `_resolve_path_for_task` before constructing `Path`:

```python
def _resolve_path_for_task(filepath: str, task_id: str = "default") -> Path:
    # Normalize MSYS paths on Windows before Path construction
    filepath = _normalize_msys_path(filepath)
    p = Path(filepath).expanduser()
    if p.is_absolute():
        return p.resolve()
    return (_resolve_base_dir(task_id) / p).resolve()
```

Where `_normalize_msys_path` reuses the existing regex pattern from `_msys_to_windows_path`, also handling `/cygdrive/` and `/mnt/` variants.

## Environment

- Windows 10/11, Git Bash (MINGW64) / MSYS2
- Hermes v0.15.x (editable install)
- CPython native (not MSYS2 Python)
