labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
### Advisory Details

**Title**: Hermes gateway quick commands bypass admin-only slash command restrictions

**Description**:

### Summary

Hermes gateway enforces `allow_admin_from` and `user_allowed_commands` only for registered gateway slash commands. Operator-configured `quick_commands` are dispatched later on a separate path without the same authorization check, which allows an authenticated allowlisted non-admin messaging user to invoke admin-only quick commands, including `type: exec` commands that run in the gateway process.

### Details

The vulnerable behavior is in `gateway/run.py`. During inbound slash-command handling, Hermes resolves the typed command and applies `_check_slash_access(...)` only when the canonical command is present in the gateway command registry:

```python
if command and canonical and is_gateway_known_command(canonical):
    _denied = self._check_slash_access(source, canonical)
    if _denied is not None:
        return _denied
```

That gate is not applied to config-backed `quick_commands`. Later in the same handler, Hermes looks up the raw typed command name in `quick_commands` and executes `type: exec` commands directly:

```python
if command in quick_commands:
    qcmd = quick_commands[command]
    if qcmd.get("type") == "exec":
        proc = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(...)
```

This creates a policy split. Registered slash commands such as `/stop` are denied for the same non-admin sender under the configured policy, but a non-registered quick command such as `/limits` still reaches the execution sink and returns command output.

I verified this with the real `GatewayRunner._handle_message(...)` entrypoint using real `SessionSource` and `MessageEvent` objects. The test policy was:

- `allow_admin_from: ["111"]`
- `user_allowed_commands: []`
- `quick_commands.limits = {type: exec, command: "printf quick-command-bypass-confirmed"}`

Under that policy, a non-admin sender `999` received `quick-command-bypass-confirmed` from `/limits`, while the control input `/stop` returned the expected denial message:

```text
⛔ /stop is admin-only here. No slash commands are enabled for non-admins on this platform.
```

### PoC

#### Prerequisites

- Hermes Agent checkout from the canonical upstream repository.
- Python virtual environment available at `./.venv`.
- A configuration equivalent to:
  - `allow_admin_from: ["111"]`
  - `user_allowed_commands: []`
  - `quick_commands.limits = {type: exec, command: "printf quick-command-bypass-confirmed"}`
- Attacker position: authenticated allowlisted non-admin gateway user in DM scope.

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Download the verification PoC from: [verification_test.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/ef5985d7985a887e1d2f4ba00394a38c)
2. Download the control PoC from: [control-non-admin-builtin-denied.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/066886bcb01b4700b5909327994701b1)
3. From the repository root, run the verification case:
   `./.venv/bin/python llm-enhance/cve-finding/similar/Auth-Privilege/GHSA-2hm8-rqrm-xfjq-quick-commands-slash-access-bypass-exp/verification_test.py`
4. Observe the verification output includes:
   `quick-command-bypass-confirmed`
5. Run the control case under the same policy:
   `./.venv/bin/python llm-enhance/cve-finding/similar/Auth-Privilege/GHSA-2hm8-rqrm-xfjq-quick-commands-slash-access-bypass-exp/control-non-admin-builtin-denied.py`
6. Observe the control output includes an admin-only denial for `/stop`.

Verification log excerpt:

{
  "mode": "Integration-Test",
  "input": "/limits",
  "user_id": "999",
  "policy": {
    "allow_admin_from": ["111"],

}

This is an authorization bypass on Hermes' messaging-gateway slash-command surface. Operators who rely on `allow_admin_from` and `user_allowed_commands` to separate admin-only and non-admin slash capabilities can unintentionally expose configured quick commands to non-admin gateway users. When the quick command uses `type: exec`, the non-admin user can trigger shell command execution in the gateway process context, subject to the operator-defined command body. That can expose sensitive operational data, modify system state, or disrupt service depending on what the quick command does.

items.body:
### Advisory Details

**Title**: Hermes browser private-network policy bypass via eval-triggered main-frame navigation

**Description**:

### Summary

Hermes' browser tooling blocks direct navigation to private or internal URLs in cloud-browser mode, but the same policy is not enforced after page-context JavaScript changes the main-frame location. An attacker who can call the standard browser tools can open a public page, use `browser_console(expression=...)` to set `location.href` to a loopback or internal target, and then read the resulting private page through `browser_snapshot()`. This is an information disclosure issue and a browser-side SSRF policy bypass.

### Details

The vulnerable logic lives in `tools/browser_tool.py`.

Hermes correctly applies private-network validation on explicit navigation:

```python
if (
    not _is_local_backend()
    and not auto_local_this_nav
    and not _allow_private_urls()
    and not _is_safe_url(url)
):
    return json.dumps({
        "success": False,
        "error": "Blocked: URL targets a private or internal address",
    })
```

It also applies a second check after redirect resolution inside `browser_navigate()`. The gap is that `browser_console()` accepts an `expression` parameter and immediately routes it to `_browser_eval()`:

```python
if expression is not None:
    return _browser_eval(expression, task_id)
```

`_browser_eval()` executes attacker-controlled JavaScript in the active page context and returns the result, but does not validate whether that JavaScript changed the main-frame URL to a private destination. After that, `browser_snapshot()` simply snapshots the active page and returns its content without re-checking the current page URL.

In practice, the attack flow is:

1. Call `browser_navigate()` on a public page to establish a live browser context.
2. Call `browser_console(expression="location.href = 'http://127.0.0.1:<port>/'; 'navigated'")`.
3. The browser loads the private loopback page.
4. Call `browser_snapshot()`.
5. Hermes returns the private page content, even though the same target would have been rejected if sent directly through `browser_navigate()`.

I verified this end-to-end against the repository's current upstream release line by running the provided PoC harness with a real local HTTP canary service and a real headless Chromium CDP endpoint. The direct-navigation control remained blocked, while the eval-driven navigation exposed the canary string `HERMES_QMWG_QPRG_3J38_CANARY` in the returned snapshot.

### PoC

#### Prerequisites

- Python 3 installed.
- Chrome or Chromium installed locally.
- Repository checkout of `https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent`.
- Ability to run the standard Hermes browser tool interface locally.
- No source modifications are required.
- The PoC harness supplies the needed environment variables automatically:
  - `BROWSERBASE_API_KEY=dummy`
  - `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID=dummy`
  - `BROWSER_CDP_URL=ws://127.0.0.1:<dynamic-port>/devtools/browser/...`

#### Reproduction Steps

1. Download the helper harness from: [common.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/5891547682fa45e63f68144bf6a61f69)
2. Download the experiment script from: [verification_test.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/267d344dd87eea6213c4b4f6612eb8ef)
3. Download the direct-navigation control from: [control-direct-navigation-block.py](https://gist.github.com/YLChen-007/77039ccb119d8d8ead21499c240737d2)
4. Place the three files in the same directory.
5. From the Hermes repository root, run the experiment:
   `python3 llm-enhance/cve-finding/similar/info_leak/Advisory-GHSA-qmwg-qprg-3j38-browser-eval-private-nav-exp/verification_test.py`
6. Run the control:
   `python3 llm-enhance/cve-finding/similar/info_leak/Advisory-GHSA-qmwg-qprg-3j38-browser-eval-private-nav-exp/control-direct-navigation-block.py`
7. Confirm the experiment returns `[DEFECT-CONFIRMED]` and the control returns `[CONTROL-BLOCKED-AS-EXPECTED]`.

### Log of Evidence

Experiment log excerpt:

```text
[DEFECT-CONFIRMED]
Verification mode: End-to-End
direct_navigation_control={"error": "Blocked: URL targets a private or internal address", "success": false}
experiment={"eval_nav": {"result": "navigated", "result_type": "str", "success": true}, "snapshot_after": {"snapshot": "- heading \"HERMES_QMWG_QPRG_3J38_CANARY\" [level=1, ref=e1]", "success": true}}
Independent observation: private canary content present after eval-driven navigation.
```

Control log excerpt:

```text
[CONTROL-BLOCKED-AS-EXPECTED]
Verification mode: End-to-End
control_result={"error": "Blocked: URL targets a private or internal address", "success": false}
Independent observation: direct private navigation was rejected by SSRF guard.
```

### Impact

This issue allows a tool-capable attacker to bypass Hermes' intended private-network browser restriction and read data from loopback or internal web endpoints that should not be reachable through the protected browser path. In real deployments, that can expose localhost-only dashboards, internal web applications, dev services, or other browser-reachable content available from the machine or network where Hermes is running. The practical impact is unauthorized disclosure of internal page content, with browser-side SSRF implications wherever Hermes is deployed with cloud-browser protections expected to block such destinations.

### Affected products

- **Ecosystem**: pip
- **Package name**: hermes-agent
- **Affected versions**: <= 0.16.0
- **Patched versions**: <None>

### Severity

- **Severity**: Medium
- **Vector string**: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N

### Weaknesses

- **CWE**: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

items.title: [Feature]: Optional Safe HTML Rendering for Chat Output
items.body:
### Problem or Use Case

Current chat interfaces are primarily text and Markdown based. While this is sufficient for most conversational needs, it becomes limiting when representing structured or UI-like information such as cards, dashboards, grouped data blocks, or multi-panel layouts.

This limitation reduces readability for complex outputs, especially in technical, data-heavy, or comparative contexts. Users are forced to mentally reconstruct structure from linear text, which increases cognitive load and reduces clarity.

The core gap is not lack of content, but lack of embedded structure inside the message flow itself.

### Proposed Solution

Introduce support for rendering sanitized HTML fragments directly inside chat messages as inline embedded components, without changing the overall chat interface or introducing separate modes.

These HTML fragments would behave like structured UI islands inside normal messages. They would appear seamlessly within the conversation flow, alongside Markdown text, not replacing it.

Key idea:
- Chat UI remains unchanged
- Messages can optionally include sandboxed HTML fragments
- HTML is strictly sanitized and whitelist-rendered (no arbitrary scripts)
- Fragments support structured layouts such as cards, tables, grouped panels, and simple visual components

This enables richer information design while preserving the linear chat experience and avoiding modal windows, popups, or external viewers.

### Alternatives Considered

1. Markdown limitations only approach
Rely solely on improved Markdown usage (tables, indentation patterns, ASCII structuring).
→ Keeps system simple and safe, but cannot express rich UI layouts or component-like structures.

2. Mode-based rendering switch
Introduce a separate rendering mode (Markdown vs HTML vs interactive).
→ Rejected because it breaks conversational continuity and forces users into context switching between display systems.

3. External or detached UI surfaces
Render structured content in separate panels, popouts, or secondary viewers outside the main chat flow.
→ Improves layout flexibility but disrupts immersion and introduces UI fragmentation.

4. Fixed component library only
Provide a strict set of predefined UI components (cards, tables, charts) without allowing raw HTML fragments.
→ Safer and more controllable, but significantly limits flexibility and extensibility for new layout types.

5. Embedded sanitized HTML fragments (preferred direction)
Allow inline, sandboxed HTML fragments embedded directly within standard chat messages, alongside Markdown.
→ Preserves conversational flow while enabling rich structured layouts without introducing separate modes or breaking the interface model.

Large (new module or significant refactor)

items.title: auxiliary auto can pair live runtime provider with stale main model

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug Description

`auxiliary.<task>.provider: auto` can combine a live main-runtime provider/client with a stale model read from global/config state.

This violates the documented default behavior that auxiliary tasks with `provider: auto` use the main chat provider + main chat model as a coherent pair.

Observed failure shape from a live install:

```text
Auxiliary auto-detect: using main provider zai (glm-5.1)
Auxiliary compression: using auto (gpt-5.5) at https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/
Failed to generate context summary: Error code: 400 - {'error': {'code': '1211', 'message': 'Unknown Model, please check the model code.'}}
```

The important part is the mismatched pair:

- client/base URL: Z.AI coding endpoint
- model sent: `gpt-5.5`

Z.AI then correctly rejects `gpt-5.5` as an unknown model. This is not a provider outage or a summarization-quality issue; it is an auxiliary routing bug.

## Expected Behavior

With default auxiliary compression config:

```yaml
auxiliary:
  compression:
    provider: auto
    model: ''
    base_url: ''
```

Hermes should route compression to the active main runtime as a coherent provider/model pair:

- main runtime `zai` + `glm-5.1` → auxiliary compression uses `zai` + `glm-5.1`
- main runtime `openai-codex` + `gpt-5.5` → auxiliary compression uses `openai-codex` + `gpt-5.5`

It should never return a client for one provider and a model from another provider.

## Actual Behavior

On current `origin/main`, `resolve_provider_client("auto", model=None, main_runtime=...)` can return the client from `_resolve_auto(main_runtime=...)` but the model from stale `_read_main_model()`.

Minimal proof against fresh upstream clone:

```python
from agent import auxiliary_client as ac

class Dummy:
    base_url = 'https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/'
    api_key = 'dummy'

orig_resolve_auto = ac._resolve_auto
orig_read_main_model = ac._read_main_model
try:
    ac._resolve_auto = lambda main_runtime=None: (Dummy(), 'glm-5.1')
    ac._read_main_model = lambda: 'gpt-5.5'  # stale config/global model

    client, model = ac.resolve_provider_client('auto', model=None, main_runtime={
        'provider': 'zai',
        'model': 'glm-5.1',
        'base_url': 'https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4',
    })

    print(model)
    print(client.base_url)
finally:
    ac._resolve_auto = orig_resolve_auto
    ac._read_main_model = orig_read_main_model
```

Current upstream result:

```text
gpt-5.5
https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/
```

Expected result:

```text
glm-5.1
https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/
```

## Root Cause

`agent/auxiliary_client.py::resolve_provider_client()` runs the universal model fallback before the `provider == "auto"` branch:

```python
if not model:
    model = _get_aux_model_for_provider(provider) or _read_main_model() or model
```

For `provider == "auto"`, `_get_aux_model_for_provider("auto")` is empty, so this can populate `model` from `_read_main_model()`.

Then the auto branch does:

```python
client, resolved = _resolve_auto(main_runtime=main_runtime)
...
final_model = model or resolved
return client, final_model
```

So `_resolve_auto(main_runtime=...)` may correctly resolve the live runtime to `zai/glm-5.1`, but `final_model` prefers stale `model` from `_read_main_model()` over the resolved live model.

This creates incoherent provider/model pairs.

## Why Existing Related Fixes Do Not Cover This

This is related to the existing auxiliary model/client mismatch bug family, but it is not the same exact bug as:

- #5803 / #5804 / #7647: cache-hit compatibility for slash-style OpenRouter model slugs sent to Codex/non-OpenRouter.
- #11289: cache-miss compatibility filter for slash-style OpenRouter model slugs on custom endpoints.
- #39047 / #39094: infer provider from an explicit provider-qualified model slug such as `google/gemini-...`.
- #12140 / #12165: regional provider model normalization for MiniMax-CN.

Those focus mostly on explicit provider-qualified/slash model slugs or cache compatibility.

This bug happens with the default config (`auxiliary.compression.model: ''`) and can involve a stale non-slash model such as `gpt-5.5`, so slash-slug compatibility filters do not catch it.

## Suspected Regression

This appears to have been introduced by:

```text
dbe5d8497200b766baab4ed1a2bbd4e2e02d3fbc
fix(auxiliary): universal main-model fallback for aux tasks (#31845)
```

That commit's intent was good: prevent OAuth auxiliary tasks from leaking to the wrong fallback provider. But applying `_read_main_model()` before `provider == "auto"` conflicts with the live-runtime routing path added earlier for compression.

## Proposed Fix

Do not prefill model from `_read_main_model()` before resolving `provider == "auto"`.

Minimal shape:

```python
if not model and provider != "auto":
    model = _get_aux_model_for_provider(provider) or _read_main_model() or model
```

Then let:

```python
client, resolved = _resolve_auto(main_runtime=main_runtime)
final_model = model or resolved
```

use the coherent model returned by `_resolve_auto()` when the user did not explicitly configure an auxiliary model.

An explicit `model` argument should still win.

## Suggested Regression Test

Add a test where:

- `provider == "auto"`
- caller passes `model=None`
- `main_runtime` is `zai/glm-5.1`
- `_read_main_model()` returns stale `gpt-5.5`
- `_resolve_auto(main_runtime)` returns `(zai_client, "glm-5.1")`

Assert that `resolve_provider_client("auto", model=None, main_runtime=...)` returns `"glm-5.1"`, not `"gpt-5.5"`.

Also assert that explicit model still wins when passed intentionally.

## Impact

When compression triggers, this can produce repeated summary failures and context degradation, for example:

```text
Auxiliary compression: using auto (gpt-5.5) at https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4/
Error code: 400 / 1211 Unknown Model
```

Users experience this as context compression being "broken" or flaky, even though the selected provider/model may be perfectly capable of compression when routed coherently.

items.title: Remote Desktop inline MEDIA audio/video renders but does not play
items.body:
## Bug Description

Hermes Desktop connected to a remote backend can render an inline media card for a backend-local `MEDIA:` audio/video file, but the player does not actually play the returned media inside the Desktop chat.

Observed with a macOS Desktop client on one MacBook connected over Tailscale/local SSH tunnel to a remote Hermes backend on another macOS machine. The assistant response included a backend-local media path under the backend Hermes home, e.g. an audio file in `audio_cache`. Desktop showed an inline audio control/card, so the UI looked like playback should work, but pressing play did not play the audio in the Desktop screen.

This is distinct from native platform delivery (Telegram voice/audio attachments) and distinct from user-local attachment upload. It is specifically the remote-backend → Desktop-client direction: the backend generated/returned a local media path, and the remote Desktop client needed to play it inline.

## Environment

- Desktop client: macOS Hermes Desktop on MacBook
- Backend/runtime: remote macOS Hermes backend reached over Tailscale/local tunnel
- Connection mode: Desktop `remote` connection
- Example media source: backend-local `MEDIA:/.../Hermes/audio_cache/<tts-file>.ogg` / `.mp3`
- App area: Hermes Desktop chat thread media rendering

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes backend/dashboard on machine B.
2. Connect Hermes Desktop on machine A to that backend via remote connection over Tailscale/local tunnel.
3. In Desktop, ask Hermes to generate or return an audio file, causing an assistant message containing a backend-local `MEDIA:` path, for example under `audio_cache`.
4. Observe the inline audio player/card in the Desktop chat thread.
5. Press play.

## Expected Behavior

Remote Desktop should fetch the backend-local media through the authenticated backend media API and play it inline using a source the Electron renderer can actually consume.

For remote connections, local filesystem schemes such as `file://...` or local-only custom streams should not be used for backend-local paths because those paths exist on the backend machine, not on the Desktop client.

## Actual Behavior

The inline audio card appears, but playback does not start / the media is not playable inside the Desktop chat.

## Investigation Notes

A local investigation found two related pitfalls:

1. The remote Desktop backend process can remain stale after a Desktop rebuild/update. Restarting only the remote Desktop/dashboard backend process made the authenticated `/api/media` route available from the client side.
2. In the Electron renderer, using a plain `/api/media?...` URL is not reliable from a `file://` renderer because it resolves against the wrong origin and cannot attach the dashboard session token. The media fetch should go through `window.hermesDesktop.api(...)`, which adds the correct auth/session context.

After authenticating through the Desktop bridge, the backend returned JSON like:

```text
200 application/json
{"data_url":"data:audio/ogg;base64,..."}
```

However, feeding large `data:audio/...` URLs directly to `<audio>` was still a weak playback path. A local patch made remote audio/video convert the authenticated `data_url` to a browser `blob:` URL before assigning it to the `<audio>` / `<video>` `src`. Images can continue to use data URLs.

## Suspected Fix Direction

In `apps/desktop/src/components/assistant-ui/markdown-text.tsx` / `apps/desktop/src/lib/media.ts`:

- Detect remote connection mode before resolving `MEDIA:` links.
- For remote backend media paths, fetch via `window.hermesDesktop.api({ path: '/api/media?path=...' })` rather than direct renderer URL or local filesystem stream.
- For remote audio/video, convert the returned `data_url` to a `Blob` and use `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` as the player source.
- Revoke the object URL on unmount.
- Keep local Desktop audio/video on the existing local streaming scheme.

## Related Issues / PRs

Related but not exact duplicates:

- #41085 — media renderer path for video/audio image-markdown
- #43630 — `/api/media` / media roots 403 errors
- #40316 — remote Desktop attachments sent as local paths (client → backend direction)
- #39447 — remote Desktop drag/drop image local-path problem (client → backend direction)
- #39290 / #39292 / #44308 — Desktop read-aloud/TTS timeout/playback latency; related voice area but different code path

## Testing Suggestions

- Unit test that in remote mode, audio/video `MEDIA:` paths call the authenticated API bridge and return a `blob:` URL for the media player.
- Unit test that images still render from the authenticated data URL.
- Backend test that `/api/media` serves audio files from allowed media roots such as `audio_cache`.
- Manual E2E: MacBook Desktop remote-connected over Tailscale to another Mac/backend; generate TTS audio; verify inline playback works in the Desktop chat thread.

- `cua-driver` upgraded from 0.3.2 to 0.5.3
- `cua-driver doctor --json`: ok
- `hermes computer-use status`: reports `cua-driver 0.5.3`

## Observed behavior

Tested with several visible, current-Space windows:

- iTerm2
- TextEdit
- Finder
- Safari

For all of them, `computer_use(action="capture", mode="som", app="...")` returned elements shaped like:

```json
{
  "index": 1,
  "role": "AXTextArea",
  "label": "...",
  "bounds": [0, 0, 0, 0]
}
```

The capture itself works, and some actions still work:

- `list_apps` works;
- `capture(mode="som", app="Safari")` works when Safari is visible in the current Space;
- `capture(mode="som", app="Finder")` works when Finder is visible in the current Space;
- `type(app="TextEdit", text="...")` can insert text into a focused `AXTextArea`.

But element geometry is always zero.

## Why this is important

The zero-bounds issue breaks the spatial grounding of SOM captures.

Even if `element_index` actions sometimes work internally through CuaDriver, the model cannot reliably:

- map AX elements to screenshot regions;
- compute coordinate fallbacks;
- reason about layout such as “the button on the right” or “the second row”;
- distinguish nearby controls;
- perform precise drag/drop or selection operations;
- verify whether an element is visible, offscreen, or spatially safe to interact with;
- avoid risky UI regions based on geometry.

This makes `computer_use` look more spatially grounded and safer than it actually is. In practice it becomes a screenshot plus textual AX tree, but without a reliable alignment between the two.

## Likely cause

In the current Hermes code, `_parse_elements_from_tree()` appears to fill bounds explicitly with zeroes:

```python
elements.append(UIElement(
    index=int(m.group(1)),
    role=m.group(2),
    label=label,
    bounds=(0, 0, 0, 0),
))
```

So this may be a Hermes parser/output limitation rather than a CuaDriver runtime limitation. If newer CuaDriver versions expose element geometry in structured output or Markdown, Hermes should parse it. If not available, the docs/schema/output should make it explicit that element bounds are unavailable for this backend.

## Expected behavior

Ideally:

- `CaptureResult.elements[*].bounds` should contain real element geometry when available;
- if geometry is unavailable, Hermes should not imply reliable coordinate/spatial targeting;
- the tool output could include a warning when all element bounds are zero;
- docs/schema should distinguish “element_index may work internally” from “bounds are available for spatial reasoning”.

## Related

Related but separate from #32766, which covers fragility around `list_windows({"on_screen_only": true})` / current-Space targeting.

# Desktop: image upload crashes renderer with `Maximum call stack size exceeded`

## Summary

Hermes Desktop crashes in the renderer when uploading an image using the image upload path. Uploading the same image as a regular file works.

This appears to be caused by `extractEmbeddedImages()` running a large global regex over a multi-megabyte `data:image/...;base64,...` preview string while rendering the optimistic user message bubble.

## Environment

- App: Hermes Desktop for Windows
- Version seen in app path: `hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/...`
- Desktop connects to a remote Hermes dashboard/gateway over SSH tunnel
- Backend/dashboard itself remains healthy; crash is in Desktop renderer

## Reproduction

1. Open Hermes Desktop on Windows.
2. Upload an image using the image upload path.
3. Renderer crashes with the error boundary screen.
4. Uploading the same image as a generic file does not crash.

## Actual behavior

Renderer crashes:

```text
[renderer console] RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
[renderer console] [error-boundary:root] RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
    at Ube (file:///C:/Users/Asad/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-CTD658G1.js:60:4078)
    at span (<anonymous>)
    at div (<anonymous>)
    at qqt (file:///C:/Users/Asad/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-CTD658G1.js:801:11091)
    ...
    at Qqt (file:///C:/Users/Asad/AppData/Local/hermes/hermes-agent/apps/desktop/release/win-unpacked/resources/app.asar/dist/assets/index-CTD658G1.js:801:11971)
    at UserMessage (<anonymous>)
```

Earlier stack frame also repeats through `UserMessage`, consistent with rendering/parsing the optimistic user message attachment preview.

## Expected behavior

Image upload should render the preview / embedded thumbnail without crashing the Desktop renderer.

## Suspected root cause

`apps/desktop/src/lib/embedded-images.ts` currently uses a global regex like this to extract base64 image URLs:

```ts
const EMBEDDED_IMAGE_RE =
  /(\{\s*"type"\s*:\s*"image_url"\s*,\s*"image_url"\s*:\s*\{\s*"url"\s*:\s*")?(data:image\/[\w.+-]+;base64,[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{64,})("\s*\}\s*\})?/g
```

For large `data:image/...;base64,...` strings generated by the image upload preview path, this can overflow the JS stack in the renderer.

## Proposed fix

Replace the large embedded-image regex extraction with an iterative scanner that:

- Finds `data:image/` occurrences with `indexOf`.
- Validates the prefix with a sticky prefix regex.
- Scans base64 characters in a simple loop.
- Preserves the previous 64-character minimum behavior.
- Handles the compact JSON `image_url` envelope.

I have a patch ready that changes:

- `apps/desktop/src/lib/embedded-images.ts`
- `apps/desktop/src/lib/embedded-images.test.ts`

Validation run locally:

```text
npm run test:ui -- src/lib/embedded-images.test.ts
✓ src/lib/embedded-images.test.ts (5 tests)

npm run typecheck
passed

npx eslint src/lib/embedded-images.ts src/lib/embedded-images.test.ts
passed
```

Patch file generated locally as:

```text
/home/asad/inbox/hermes-desktop-image-upload-fix.patch
```

The patch adds a regression test with a 2.5MB data URL:

```ts
it('handles multi-megabyte image data URLs without recursive regex overflow', () => {
  const large = 'data:image/jpeg;base64,' + 'A'.repeat(2_500_000)
  const result = extractEmbeddedImages(`before ${large} after`)

  expect(result.cleanedText).toBe('before  after')
  expect(result.images).toHaveLength(1)
  expect(result.images[0]).toHaveLength(large.length)
})
```

items.title: Flaky test: notification-poller dedup test fails when poller threads leaked by earlier tests race on the global completion_queue
items.body:
## Summary

`tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py::test_notification_poller_emits_distinct_watch_matches_once` is flaky in CI: it can fail with `AssertionError: assert 3 == 2` (one extra `status.update` emission). The root cause is a test-isolation gap, not the dedup logic itself: **notification-poller threads leaked by earlier tests in the same pytest process race on the global `process_registry.completion_queue`**, and each poller thread keeps its own `_emitted` dedup set, so an exact-replay event consumed by a *different* (leaked) poller thread is not deduped.

## Observed failure

Seen on PR #44061, run [27404366238](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/actions/runs/27404366238) `test (6)` (the test itself is unmodified there):

```
__________ test_notification_poller_emits_distinct_watch_matches_once __________
>           assert len(status_calls) == 2
E           AssertionError: assert 3 == 2
E            +  where 3 = len([('status.update', '0abe5e79', {'command': 'tail -f app.log', 'event_type': 'watch_match', ...}),
                               ...
                               ('status.update', 'ec783fb7', {'command': 'tail -f app.log', 'event_type': 'watch_match', ...})])
```

## Smoking gun

The test starts its own poller with `sid_watch_dedup`, yet the captured emissions carry sids `0abe5e79` and `ec783fb7` — sessions from *earlier tests*. The mechanism:

1. Any test that exercises the session-init paths starts a daemon poller via `_start_notification_poller` (`tui_gateway/server.py`); the only handles to stop it are the returned `stop` event stored as `_sessions[sid]["_notif_stop"]` and the session's `_finalized` flag.
2. Tests typically clean up with `server._sessions.pop(sid)` — which removes the dict entry but never sets the stop event or `_finalized`, so the thread keeps polling `process_registry.completion_queue.get(timeout=0.5)` for the rest of the pytest process.
3. The leaked threads call `server._emit` dynamically, so they emit through whatever monkeypatch the *currently running* test installed.
4. The dedup test drains the queue and enqueues 3 `watch_match` events (2 distinct + 1 exact replay) whose process `session_id` (`proc_watch_dedup`) is owned by no live session, so `_notification_event_belongs_elsewhere` lets any poller consume them. Whichever mix of the test's own drain pass and leaked threads consumes them, the replay lands in a thread with a fresh `_emitted` set → 3 emissions instead of 2.

The per-thread `_emitted` set is fine in production (one poller per session); only the cross-test thread leak breaks the invariant.

## Suggested fixes (either suffices)

- Test-side: an autouse fixture in `tests/test_tui_gateway_server.py` that wraps `_start_notification_poller`, records every returned stop event, and sets them all at teardown (popping `_sessions` alone does not stop the thread). Patching `completion_queue` per-test does **not** help — the loop re-reads the attribute every iteration, so leaked threads would consume from the fresh queue too.
- Server-side: have `_notification_poller_loop` also exit when its `sid` is no longer in `_sessions`, which makes the existing `_sessions.pop(...)` cleanup sufficient and also reaps pollers for dead sessions in production.

Happy to PR whichever direction is preferred.

# Issue: Desktop client process leak when switching to non-default profiles + feature request

## Bug: Process leak when switching profiles

**Description:**
When clicking on a non-default profile in the desktop client, the client spawns new `python.exe` dashboard processes (with `--open-profile <name>`) on every connection attempt but **never cleans up old ones** when the connection fails. This causes an exponential process leak that exhausts system resources and degrades performance for ALL profiles, including the default one.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create a non-default profile: `hermes profile create orchestrator --clone`
2. Open the desktop client
3. Click on the non-default profile to switch to it
4. Observe "Gateway Offline" and connection timeout
5. Check process count: `tasklist | findstr python` — new processes accumulate on every retry

**Expected behavior:**
- Failed dashboard processes should be cleaned up immediately
- Connection retries should reuse existing processes, not spawn new ones

**Actual behavior:**
- Each retry spawns 2 new `python.exe` processes (one per port increment)
- Old processes are never killed
- After a few minutes, 100+ zombie processes accumulate (~120MB each)
- System runs out of resources, default profile also becomes slow/unresponsive

**Environment:**
- OS: Windows 11
- Hermes version: 0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
- Model: mimo-v2.5-pro (xiaomi)
- Profiles: 1 default + 1 non-default

**Workaround:**
Manually kill excess processes:
```bash
wmic process where "name='python.exe' and commandline like '%dashboard%'" get processid | ...
```

---

## Feature Request: Chat with non-default profiles in desktop client

**Description:**
The desktop client currently shows "Gateway Offline" for non-default profiles that have no messaging platforms configured, and **disables the chat input box**. However, the client's own chat mechanism (TUI/PTY) does NOT require a messaging platform — this was confirmed working for the default profile.

**Request:**
Allow chatting with non-default profiles from the desktop client, regardless of whether they have messaging platforms configured. The TUI/PTY-based chat should work the same way it does for the default profile.

**Use case:**
Users create specialized profiles (e.g., `coder`, `orchestrator`, `reviewer`) with different models and SOUL.md personalities, and want to interact with them directly from the desktop client without having to configure messaging platforms for each one.

**Current workaround:**
Use CLI: `hermes -p <profile> chat`

items.body:
## Bug Description

When using the `/compress` command in a long conversation, the original messages in `state.db` are permanently deleted and replaced with only the compressed summary (~7 messages). Hundreds of conversation messages are lost.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start a long conversation (enough messages to compress)
2. Run `/compress` command
3. Check `state.db` — the original session now only contains compressed messages

## Expected Behavior

Original messages should be preserved. The compressed session should be written to a **new** session with `parent_session_id` pointing to the old one, so `session_search` can still find the full transcript.

## Actual Behavior

`rewrite_transcript()` is called **unconditionally** on the original session ID, which calls `replace_messages()` → `DELETE FROM messages` → inserts only the compressed messages. The original hundreds of messages are permanently gone.

## Root Cause

This is the same underlying issue as #39704 (Session Hygiene compression), but triggered by the manual `/compress` command.

The session rotation logic in `conversation_compression.py` is gated on `agent._session_db` being truthy:

```python
if agent._session_db:  # ← If None, entire session rotation is SKIPPED
    agent._session_db.end_session(agent.session_id, "compression")
    agent.session_id = f"{datetime.now().strftime(...)}_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
    agent._session_db.create_session(...)
```

But `rewrite_transcript()` in the calling code executes **regardless** of whether rotation happened:

```python
# This executes UNCONDITIONALLY:
self.session_store.rewrite_transcript(
    session_entry.session_id, _compressed  # ← Overwrites original session!
)
```

When `_session_db` is `None`, no new session is created, no old session is ended, and `rewrite_transcript()` overwrites the original session with compressed content.

## Impact

- Long conversations lose their full history
- `session_search` can no longer find the original messages
- Only the compressed summary (~7 messages) remains

## Environment

- Hermes Agent latest (fork: UniGood/hermes-agent)
- Platform: Weixin/WeChat
- Model: mimo-v2.5-pro
- Platform: Linux

## Related

- #39704 — Same root cause, triggered by automatic Session Hygiene compression
- #39731 — Official fix PR (still OPEN)
- #40112 — Alternative fix PR (still OPEN)
- #39745 — Pass session_db to hygiene agent (still OPEN)

All three fix PRs are still unmerged. The manual `/compress` command suffers from the same bug.

items.title: [Bug]: _try_wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE silently swallows exceptions, corrupts state.db WAL to zero bytes

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: sweeper:risk-session-state
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may lose/corrupt/mis-associate session or context state

items.body:
## Bug Description

`SessionDB._try_wal_checkpoint()` in `hermes_state.py` performs a `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` that truncates the WAL file to zero bytes, then catches ALL exceptions with a bare `except Exception: pass`. If the checkpoint fails mid-operation (e.g., due to FTS write contention, transient I/O error, or memory provider's concurrent activity), the WAL is already truncated to zero but the data was not fully written back to the main DB. The next connection attempt hits `sqlite3.OperationalError: disk I/O error` and the entire state.db becomes unusable — cascading to TUI session store, holographic memory provider, and SessionDB.

**This is a data-loss class bug.** The checkpoint is destructive (TRUNCATE) with no rollback or error recovery path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run Hermes Desktop with holographic memory provider enabled (uses `memory_store.db` via the same `apply_wal_with_fallback` code path)
2. Have an agent session that triggers multiple `memory` tool writes (e.g., `fact_store` or `memory` tool calls)
3. After 50 writes, `_try_wal_checkpoint` runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`
4. If any transient error occurs during checkpoint (lock contention, FTS trigger conflict, I/O hiccup), the exception is silently swallowed — WAL is zero bytes, but DB is inconsistent
5. On next connection attempt: `TUI session store unavailable — continuing without state.db features: disk I/O error`

**Observed in production:** 2026-06-12, state.db-wal became 0 bytes at 16:48, state.db-shm timestamp was from 15:07 (stale), and all three components failed simultaneously: TUI session store, holographic memory, and SessionDB. The memory tool had failed 4 consecutive times in a prior turn, triggering the "looks like a loop" warning before the cascade failure.

## Expected Behavior

`_try_wal_checkpoint` should never silently swallow exceptions from a destructive TRUNCATE checkpoint. At minimum:
- Log the error (even if non-fatal)
- Verify DB integrity after a failed checkpoint before proceeding
- Or use `PASSIVE` checkpoint (which never truncates) and reserve TRUNCATE for explicit shutdown/pragma optimize

## Actual Behavior

```python
# hermes_state.py:870-881
def _try_wal_checkpoint(self) -> None:
    try:
        with self._lock:
            result = self._conn.execute(
                "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)"
            ).fetchone()
            ...
    except Exception:
        pass  # Best effort — never fatal.
```

The `pass` silently discards all errors. Combined with TRUNCATE (which zeroes the WAL file), this is a data-loss hazard.

## Root Cause Analysis

1. `_try_wal_checkpoint` uses `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` which truncates WAL to **zero bytes** (hermes_state.py:873, docstring confirms "truncates the WAL file to zero bytes")
2. The `except Exception: pass` at line 880 silently swallows ANY error during or after the TRUNCATE
3. SQLite's FTS5 virtual tables (used by state.db's session search index) can desync during interrupted checkpoints — this is documented in issue #33865
4. Multiple components share the same checkpoint path: state.db (SessionDB + TUI session store) and memory_store.db (holographic provider), so a failure in any component's write path can trigger a destructive checkpoint that damages the DB

The existing fix in PR #31294 (removing "disk i/o error" from `_WAL_INCOMPAT_MARKERS`) only addresses WAL→DELETE fallback corruption — it does NOT address the unrelated corruption path through `_try_wal_checkpoint`.

## Proposed Fix

Two changes needed in `hermes_state.py`:

1. **Never silently swallow checkpoint errors** — log the exception at warning level:
```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning("WAL checkpoint failed (non-fatal): %s", e)
```

2. **Add integrity guard after failed checkpoint** — if TRUNCATE checkpoint raised, verify the DB is still usable before continuing:
```python
except Exception as e:
    logger.warning("WAL checkpoint failed: %s", e)
    try:
        self._conn.execute("PRAGMA quick_check")
    except Exception:
        logger.error("state.db integrity check failed after checkpoint error — DB may be corrupted")
```

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10
- **Hermes version:** 0.16.0
- **Python:** 3.14.2
- **Memory provider:** holographic
- **File system:** NTFS (C: drive, 130G free)
- **state.db size:** ~38MB (WAL mode)

## Related Issues / PRs

- #33865 — FTS corruption during checkpoint silently swallowed (same `except Exception: pass` pattern noted)
- PR #31294 — Removed EIO from WAL incompatibility markers (different corruption path)
- PR #31208 — SQLite hardening with secure_delete + synchronous=FULL
- #30445 — Multi-gateway concurrent SQLite access corruption risk

labels.name: comp/cli

items.body:
## Bug Description

`/codex-runtime on` can still fail in the macOS Desktop app when `codex` is installed by Homebrew at `/opt/homebrew/bin/codex`.

The Desktop dashboard backend now needs the same class of POSIX PATH completion as the terminal tool path. A macOS GUI-launched Desktop backend may have a PATH that includes Hermes-managed bins and the standard Apple paths, while still missing Apple Silicon Homebrew:

```text
~/.hermes/node/bin:<venv>/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/usr/local/bin
```

In that environment, `agent/transports/codex_app_server.py::check_codex_binary()` calls `subprocess.run(["codex", "--version"])` and fails with `FileNotFoundError` when the only installed `codex` binary is in `/opt/homebrew/bin`.

## Relation to existing issues / PRs

- #35613 / #42653 fixed the same class of macOS PATH issue for terminal/gateway subprocesses by appending missing POSIX sane PATH entries individually.
- #41385 / #41389 covers the Desktop dashboard backend missing `~/.hermes/node/bin` for Hermes-managed Node binaries.
- This issue is the remaining Desktop backend branch: after adding Hermes-managed Node and venv bins, the backend still needs `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/sbin`, and the other POSIX sane fallback entries so Homebrew-installed CLIs are discoverable too.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On Apple Silicon macOS, install Codex with Homebrew so `codex` resolves as `/opt/homebrew/bin/codex`.
2. Ensure there is no `codex` binary under `~/.hermes/node/bin`.
3. Launch Hermes Desktop from Finder/Dock or another GUI path that does not inherit a login-shell PATH.
4. Run `/codex-runtime on`.

## Expected Behavior

The Desktop dashboard backend PATH includes the Hermes-managed Node bin, the venv bin, and missing POSIX sane entries such as:

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin
/opt/homebrew/sbin
/usr/local/sbin
/usr/local/bin
/usr/sbin
/usr/bin
/sbin
/bin
```

`/codex-runtime on` should discover the Homebrew-installed `codex` binary and enable `codex_app_server`.

## Actual Behavior

The Desktop backend PATH can omit `/opt/homebrew/bin`, so `/codex-runtime on` reports:

```text
Cannot enable codex_app_server runtime: codex CLI not found at 'codex'. Install with: npm i -g @openai/codex
```

## Proposed Fix

Add a testable Desktop backend env helper that:

- prepends Hermes-managed bins (`~/.hermes/node/bin`, venv bin), following the direction in #41389;
- appends missing POSIX sane PATH entries individually, following the terminal fix from #42653;
- preserves caller PATH precedence and avoids duplicates;
- preserves Windows PATH casing and delimiters.

I have a working patch with Node regression tests and will open a PR against this issue.

Change the dropdown options from `["ask", "yolo", "deny"]` to `["manual", "smart", "off"]` to match the actual engine values.

- Hermes version: current main

- Platforms affected: Web dashboard config → all downstream platforms

## Describe the bug

When `agent.reasoning_effort` is set to `none` in `config.yaml`, the Desktop UI correctly shows the thinking switch as **off** on a fresh session. However, after sending the first message, the switch jumps back to **on** (medium) automatically.

## To Reproduce

1. Set `agent.reasoning_effort: none` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`
2. Restart Hermes Desktop
3. Start a new session → thinking toggle shows **off** ✅
4. Send any message
5. After response, open model menu → thinking toggle is now **on** (medium) ❌

## Root cause analysis

The chain of events:

1. `useHermesConfig` (`use-hermes-config.ts:59-62`) correctly reads `reasoning_effort: none` from config.yaml on startup, setting `currentReasoningEffort` to `"none"` when no active session exists.
2. When a session is established, `onSessionInfo` (`use-session-actions.ts:306-309`) overwrites it with the server-returned `reasoning_effort` — which appears to be `""` (empty) or `"medium"` rather than respecting the config value.
3. `normalizeEffort` (`model-edit-submenu.ts:244`) has a fallback to `"medium"` for unrecognized/empty values: `return EFFORT_OPTIONS.some(option => option.value === value) ? value : "medium"`.

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

items.body:
## Summary

Gateway warm sessions can accumulate merged `\n\n`-joined user blobs in the model payload while platform inbound stays single-message per turn.

## Observed behavior (reporter session `20260612_085708_c4403c61`, 2026-06-12 weixin)

| Layer | Evidence |
|-------|----------|
| Gateway inbound | Single message each turn |
| Agent `turn_context` | `history=N msg='…'` single string |
| AxonHub `requests` | Last `user` content grows: 2 → 3 → … → 6 segments joined with `\n\n` |
| Alternation repair | `Repaired N message-alternation violations` monotonically increasing |

Minimal repro segment **13:15–13:17 CST**:

- **13:15:41** — Turn ended `last_msg_role=assistant`, reply sent to WeChat; AxonHub request #246 tail is correct (`user → assistant → tool → assistant`).
- **13:17:20** — Next inbound single user message; AxonHub #252 tail shows assistant/tool chain **321–323 gone**, last user already **two messages merged**.
- `turn_context` history count: 342 → **343 (+1 only)** — only the inbound user row landed in `state.db`, not the assistant/tool chain.

Cache eviction after ~1h idle was an **amplifier**, not the root cause (blob already 5 segments before evict).

## Root cause chain

1. `turn_context` **early-persists** inbound user at turn start → `_last_flushed_db_idx` advances past pre-turn length.
2. First API call runs `repair_message_sequence()` which **merges consecutive users** (orphan + new) and **shrinks** `messages` in place.
3. Flush cursor stays at the pre-compaction index → turn-end `_flush_messages_to_session_db` computes `flush_from` **past the first post-repair assistant row** and skips persisting the assistant/tool chain.
4. Next turn loads orphan user → new user → repair merges again → blob grows.

#44327 (reset `_last_flushed_db_idx` on cached-agent fresh turns) is **necessary** but **not sufficient** when step 2 compacts within the same turn.

## Proposed fix

- After `repair_message_sequence` compacts the list, clamp `_last_flushed_db_idx` to `len(messages)`.
- In `_flush_messages_to_session_db`, if cursor overshoots list length, fall back to `start_idx`.
- Include #44327 cached-agent cursor reset.

items.title: MCP OAuth /oauth/start polls 30s on probe failure instead of returning immediately

labels.name: sweeper:implemented-on-main
labels.description: Sweeper: behavior already present on current main

items.body:
## Bug

When `POST /api/mcp/servers/{name}/oauth/start` triggers an OAuth flow that fails before generating an `authorization_url` (e.g. DCR returns 404 for providers like GitHub that don't support Dynamic Client Registration), the endpoint polls for the full 30 seconds before returning `{"status": "timeout"}` instead of returning `{"status": "failed"}` immediately.

## Root Cause

Two issues in `hermes_cli/web_server.py` `start_mcp_oauth()`:

1. **Silent exception swallowing**: The inner `_connect_and_auth()` coroutine catches all exceptions with `except Exception: pass`, so probe failures are never surfaced to the polling loop. The `_probe_result` status remains `"redirect_triggered"` even after the flow dies.

2. **No completion signal**: There is no mechanism for the probe thread to tell the main polling loop that it has finished. The loop only checks `_probe_result["status"] in ("failed",)` — but status is never set to `"failed"` by the coroutine (only by the outer try/except around thread setup).

### Timeline

```
T+0s    POST /oauth/start → clears tokens, starts probe thread
T+0.5s  Probe: _connect_server → 401 → SDK async_auth_flow
T+1s    SDK Step 1: PRM discovery → 404
T+1.5s  SDK Step 2: OASM discovery → 404
T+2s    SDK Step 4: DCR /register → 404 → raises OAuthRegistrationError
T+2s    _connect_and_auth: except Exception: pass ← error swallowed!
T+2s    Probe thread exits, but _probe_result["status"] == "redirect_triggered"
T+2s→T+30s  Main loop polls every 0.5s, waiting for authorization_url that will never appear
T+30s   Timeout → returns {"status": "timeout"}  ← should be "failed"
```

## Fix

Two changes to `start_mcp_oauth()` in `hermes_cli/web_server.py`:

1. Replace `except Exception: pass` with error capture that sets `_probe_result["status"] = "failed"` and `_probe_result["error"]`.

2. Add a `threading.Event` (`_probe_done`) that the coroutine sets in a `finally` block. The polling loop checks `_probe_done.is_set()` — if the probe finished without producing an `authorization_url`, it breaks immediately and returns `{"status": "failed"}`.

With this fix, the GitHub OAuth failure returns in ~2s instead of 30s.

## Environment

- hermes-agent latest (commit with MCP OAuth support)
- Multi-user broker mode with nginx reverse proxy
- MCP servers configured with `auth: oauth` (confirmed with GitHub and Notion)

items.title: [Bug]: RotatingFileHandler.doRollover() raises PermissionError [WinError 32] on Windows — uncaught, spams stderr on every emit

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Bug Description

On Windows, the logger configured in `hermes_logging.py` raises
`PermissionError [WinError 32]` from inside `RotatingFileHandler.doRollover()`
on every rotation attempt. Because the exception is not caught, the stdlib
`logging` module's default error handler prints a full Python traceback to
stderr on every subsequent log emit. The agent loop continues to function
correctly, but the stderr stream and `agent.log` itself become flooded
with the same traceback repeated dozens of times per turn, which:

1. Obscures real errors in log monitoring
2. Makes it look like Hermes is crashing when it is not
3. Fails the goal of log rotation entirely — the file is never actually
   rotated, so it sits pinned at the size threshold until the gateway
   restarts

### Affected Component

- Agent Core (conversation loop, context compression, memory)
- CLI entry point (`hermes_logging.py` is loaded by the CLI, gateway, and
  TUI processes; `agent.log` is the symptom visible to all three)

### Operating System

Windows 10 (native, MSYS2/Git Bash) — also reproducible on Windows 11.

### Python Version

3.11.15

### Hermes Version

`bfd5f8e4e` (60+ commits behind `main` as of June 12, 2026), but the
behaviour is unchanged on current `main` — `hermes_logging.py` still uses
stdlib `RotatingFileHandler` via `_ManagedRotatingFileHandler`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Hermes on Windows 10/11 (native install, not WSL)
2. Run a busy session: `hermes chat` with parallel tool use, or run
   `hermes gateway` + a TUI session simultaneously
3. Generate enough log volume to cross the 5 MiB rotation threshold
   (one or two long agent turns is usually enough)
4. Observe stderr (or `tail -f ~/.hermes/logs/agent.log`)

## Expected Behavior

`agent.log` rotates to `agent.log.1` when it exceeds `maxBytes`.
No tracebacks on stderr. Logging is silent on success.

## Actual Behavior

`agent.log` is pinned at exactly the rotation threshold. The same
`PermissionError [WinError 32]` traceback is printed to stderr on
every subsequent log emit. State from a real session today (2026-06-12):

```text
agent.log      5,242,863 bytes   (sitting at 5 MiB threshold, not rotated)
agent.log.1    (missing)
agent.log.2    (missing)
agent.log.3    5,402,188 bytes   (last successful rotation — 2 days ago)
errors.log     1,047,988 bytes   (rotating fine, same handler)
```

Representative traceback (one of dozens, abridged):

```text
PermissionError: [WinError 32] The process cannot access the file
because it is being used by another process:
'C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\hermes\\logs\\agent.log'
-> 'C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\hermes\\logs\\agent.log.1'

  File "...\\logging\\handlers.py", line 115, in rotate
    os.rename(source, dest)
  File "...\\logging\\handlers.py", line 179, in doRollover
    self.rotate(self.baseFilename, dfn)
  File "...\\hermes_logging.py", line 470, in doRollover
    super().doRollover()
  File "...\\hermes_logging.py", line 462, in emit
    super().emit(record)
```

## Root Cause

`hermes_logging.py` defines `_ManagedRotatingFileHandler`, a thin
subclass of stdlib `logging.handlers.RotatingFileHandler` whose
`doRollover()` override at line 469–474 is:

```python
def doRollover(self):
    super().doRollover()   # ← stdlib raises PermissionError here on Windows
    self._chmod_if_managed()
    self._record_stream_stat()
```

The override exists to re-stat and chmod after rollover, but it does not
catch the exception. The stdlib `doRollover()` calls
`os.rename(self.baseFilename, dfn)` to atomically swap `agent.log` →
`agent.log.1`. On POSIX this is an inode swap and succeeds even when
other handles have the source open. **On Windows, `os.rename` requires
exclusive access to the source — any open append-mode handle blocks
it with `WinError 32`.** Hermes runs as multiple OS processes — TUI,
gateway, `hy_memory` server, MCP servers, on-demand CLI commands —
each with its own file descriptor on `agent.log`. Within a single
process, threads share the same FD and don't block each other from
renaming. Across processes, each has its own FD, and Windows refuses
to rename a file another process has open unless that process opened
it with `FILE_SHARE_DELETE` (which CPython's `open(path, 'a')` does
not request). So the bug is cross-process, not cross-thread.
The rename fails, the override propagates the exception, stdlib's
`Handler.handleError` prints the traceback, and the file size is
unchanged — so the next `emit()` re-triggers the rollover check and
the loop continues indefinitely.

## Proposed Fix

One change. A second change — wrapping `super().doRollover()` in
`try/except PermissionError` as defense-in-depth — was originally
proposed alongside this one, but is redundant once the base-class
swap is in: `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler.doRollover()` only raises
if its internal lock cannot be acquired within `lock_timeout` (default
5s), which doesn't happen in normal multi-process operation. A
`try/except` would only hide a (loud) stderr if the lock ever did
fail — leaving the exception to propagate is the right behavior.

### 1. Swap the underlying handler (the real fix)

`concurrent-log-handler` (PyPI, Apache-2.0, 110M+ downloads, latest
0.9.29 Feb 2026 — used by Django, AWS CLI, etc. for exactly this case)
provides `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler` with the same constructor
signature as `RotatingFileHandler`. On Windows it uses
copy-then-truncate instead of rename, which works while other threads
hold the source open. On POSIX it keeps the atomic rename.

```python
# hermes_logging.py
- from logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler
- class _ManagedRotatingFileHandler(RotatingFileHandler): ...
+ try:
+     from concurrent_log_handler import ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler as _BaseRotatingHandler
+ except ImportError:  # graceful fallback if the dep is not installed
+     from logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler as _BaseRotatingHandler
+ class _ManagedRotatingFileHandler(_BaseRotatingHandler): ...
```

## Why this is a new issue, not a duplicate of #31050

[#31050](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/31050) reported
this problem as "Issue 2" of three Windows issues bundled together,
alongside an SGR mouse leak (Issue 1) and a console window flash
(Issue 3). The whole ticket was bulk-closed as a duplicate of #18658
(mouse leak) during a triage sweep, even though maintainer @alt-glitch
specifically noted on the ticket that the three issues
*"could be split into separate tickets for tracking"* and that Issue 2
was *"related to #27649"* — not to #18658. Issue 2 was never actually
tracked as its own ticket, and no PR has been filed to fix it.

This new issue is intentionally scoped to the single, still-unfixed
PermissionError on Windows so it cannot be misclosed as a dup of the
mouse-leak ticket. The mouse-leak (#18658) and console-flash (#30206)
issues are out of scope here.

## See also

- **#31050** — original bundled report, closed; log-rotation sub-issue
  never tracked separately
- **#27649** — related but distinct: *multi-process* writes landing in
  the wrong file after rotation. P3, different fix surface
  (multi-process file locking, not single-process Windows rename). A
  complete fix to the logger will likely touch both, but they should
  remain separate issues for triage

## Verification

End-to-end test of fix #1 alone applied locally:

- **20 interleaved emits across 2 independent `_ManagedRotatingFileHandler` instances on the same file** (simulates two Hermes processes both writing to and rotating the same log): 0 exceptions, 0 stderr, clean rotation producing `agent.log.1` / `.2` / `.3` backups + the `.__agent.lock` sidecar that `concurrent-log-handler` uses for cross-process coordination
- **`hermes --version`, `hermes --help`, full plugin-discovery commands**: all run with zero `--- Logging error ---` blocks on stderr
- **The `as RotatingFileHandler` alias pattern works**: the `isinstance(h, RotatingFileHandler)` checks in `_add_rotating_handler` (dedup) and `setup_verbose_logging` (verbose-mode handler) continue to match without modification

This is in addition to the 8-thread × 80-emit (640 records) test noted in the comment thread, which validated the same fix from a multi-threaded angle.

## Additional context

- No existing PRs reference `concurrent-log-handler` or
  `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler` in the repo
- The change is just the import at line 35 + the class declaration that
  consumes it. The existing `doRollover()` override at line 469 stays
  as-is — no defense-in-depth `try/except` is needed once the base
  class is swapped, because `ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler` only raises
  on lock-acquisition timeout (5s default), which is a real bug to
  surface rather than suppress
- Happy to submit a PR with the import + class-swap change plus a
  regression test that simulates concurrent file access on a Windows
  runner. Just confirm the target branch (`main`? or `dev` per
  AGENTS.md — verifying with `git ls-remote --heads origin` is
  suggested before opening the PR)
- Error path is non-functional in the strict sense (the agent works),
  but the noise-to-signal ratio in `agent.log` makes real debugging
  difficult — this is a real Windows-user-facing papercut that affects
  every install once logs reach 5 MiB

router, nous, local/custom, api-key. The '_try_openrouter()' function only succeeds

```

Apparently this is coming from the fallback sequence and fallback is desired, but why it is defaulting to Gemini 3 Flash? i am currently digging in Hermes code to see if it is hard-coded in there or was a consequence of the `routing`  feature of open router.

line 486:

```

----
 
1. title_generator.py calls call_llm(task="title_generation")
2. call_llm() calls _resolve_task_provider_model(task="title_generation") → no per-task config → returns ("auto", None, None, None, None)
3. call_llm() calls _get_cached_client("auto", None, ...)
4. _get_cached_client() → resolve_provider_client(provider="auto", ...)
5. resolve_provider_client() → _resolve_auto()_resolve_auto() has a 2-step chain:

Step 1: Main provider (custom at http://host:port/v1). The _try_custom_endpoint() function checks if not custom_base or not custom_key: return None, None. Your api_key: none is YAML None, so this fails.

Step 2: The hardcoded fallback chain in order:

2. _try_nous() — checks Nous auth.
3. _try_custom_endpoint() — already failed in Step 1.
4. _try_anthropic() — checks Anthropic key.

The model is hardcoded at line 486:

python

When _try_openrouter() succeeds (OPENROUTER_API_KEY is set), it returns _OPENROUTER_MODEL as the model. That's where gemini-3-flash-preview came from.  — it's a deliberate hardcoded fallback model for OpenRouter in the auxiliary client.

The presence of OPENROUTER_API_KEY caused Step 2 to route to OpenRouter with the hardcoded gemini-3-flash-preview model. # feat(delegation): add model override to delegate_task

## Pre-flight Checks
- [x] I have searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate
- [x] I understand this issue needs status:approved before a PR can be opened

## Problem Description

`delegate_task` currently has no `model` parameter. Sub-agents always inherit the parent session's model. This forces all work through a single model regardless of task characteristics.

Different tasks have different strengths. Reasoning-heavy work (specs, design, architecture) benefits from frontier models (Claude, GPT-4o, Gemini Pro). Mechanical implementation (file edits, test writing, refactors) performs well with faster/cheaper coding models. Review and verification benefit from a fresh perspective, sometimes literally a different model's "eyes."

Without per-delegation model selection, users must either:
- Run expensive frontier models for everything (wasteful)
- Run fast models for everything (quality loss on hard reasoning)
- Manually switch sessions per task type (breaks orchestration flow)

## Proposed Solution

Add an optional `model` parameter to `delegate_task`:

```json
{
  "goal": "Write delta spec for auth-middleware change",
  "model": {
    "provider": "anthropic",
    "model": "claude-sonnet-4"
  }
}
```

When provided, the sub-agent runs on the specified model instead of inheriting the parent's. When omitted, current behavior (inherit) is preserved.

This mirrors the existing `model` override pattern in `cronjob`, which already supports per-job model selection.

## Affected Area

Other (agent delegation subsystem)

## Use Case: SDD Orchestration

The SDD (Spec-Driven Development) workflow runs 10 phases with very different cognitive profiles:

| Phase | Optimal Model Profile |
|-------|----------------------|
| explore, propose, spec, design | Strong reasoning, nuanced judgment |
| tasks | Balanced reasoning + structure |
| apply | Fast coding, file editing |
| verify | Independent review perspective |
| sync, archive | Mechanical, low reasoning needed |

A per-phase model config in `openspec/config.yaml` would let the orchestrator pick the right tool for each phase, but that only works if `delegate_task` can accept the override.

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Manual session switching** — breaks the SDD orchestration flow, defeats the purpose of an orchestrator
2. **`cronjob` one-shot per phase** — loses interactive gates and approval workflow between phases
3. **Model routing inside skills** — skills don't control model selection, only the delegation layer can

items.title: WebUI native server serves large JS assets slowly due to on-the-fly Brotli compression
items.body:
## Bug description

Hermes WebUI's native Node.js server on port 8648 can take several seconds to serve large hashed JS assets to real browsers because the browser advertises Brotli support (`Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br`) and the server appears to Brotli-compress the multi-MB JS response on the fly before sending the first byte.

This makes Chrome DevTools show a very long `Waiting for server response` time for files such as Mermaid and Monaco bundles, even on localhost.

## Reproduction

Environment:
- OS: Windows 10
- Hermes WebUI: `hermes-web-ui 0.6.14`
- Native WebUI URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8648`
- Example asset: `/assets/js/mermaid-CWQI515T.js`
- Asset size on disk: ~3.1 MB

Requests without browser-style compression are fast:

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null \
  -w "TTFB=%{time_starttransfer}s Total=%{time_total}s Size=%{size_download}\n" \
  http://127.0.0.1:8648/assets/js/mermaid-CWQI515T.js
```

Observed locally: milliseconds.

Python test without `Accept-Encoding`:

```python
import time, urllib.request
req = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8648/assets/js/mermaid-CWQI515T.js')
t0 = time.time()
resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req)
t1 = time.time()
data = resp.read()
t2 = time.time()
print('TTFB ms', (t1-t0)*1000, 'download ms', (t2-t1)*1000, 'size', len(data), 'encoding', resp.headers.get('Content-Encoding'))
```

Observed locally:

```text
TTFB: ~5.5ms
Download: ~10.5ms
Total: ~16ms
Encoding: none
Size: 3187484 bytes
```

Python test with browser-like `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br`:

```python
import time, urllib.request
req = urllib.request.Request('http://127.0.0.1:8648/assets/js/mermaid-CWQI515T.js')
req.add_header('User-Agent', 'Mozilla/5.0 Chrome')
req.add_header('Accept', '*/*')
req.add_header('Accept-Encoding', 'gzip, deflate, br')
t0 = time.time()
resp = urllib.request.urlopen(req)
t1 = time.time()
data = resp.read()
t2 = time.time()
print('TTFB ms', (t1-t0)*1000, 'download ms', (t2-t1)*1000, 'size', len(data), 'encoding', resp.headers.get('Content-Encoding'))
```

Observed locally:

```text
TTFB: ~6740ms
Download: ~8ms
Total: ~6748ms
Encoding: br
Size: 659911 bytes
```

Python test with `Accept-Encoding: gzip` only:

```text
TTFB: ~9ms
Download: ~86ms
Total: ~95ms
Encoding: gzip
```

Chrome DevTools shows the same shape: `Waiting for server response` is ~6-8s, while `Content Download` is short.

## Expected behavior

Hashed production assets such as:

- `mermaid-CWQI515T.js`
- `monaco-editor-YM0cdSGX.js`

should load quickly and should not block the Node.js server for seconds on localhost.

Recommended behavior:

1. Do not Brotli-compress large JS assets on the fly.
2. Either:
   - serve precompressed `.br` / `.gz` files generated at build time, or
   - use gzip only for dynamic compression, or
   - disable compression for large static assets on the Node server.
3. Since these asset filenames are content-hashed, return long-lived immutable cache headers, e.g.:

```http
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
```

## Actual behavior

The native 8648 Node.js server appears to choose Brotli when browsers send `Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br`. For multi-MB bundles, the server spends seconds before the first byte is sent.

Also, the native response currently uses short/no effective caching for assets, for example:

```http
Cache-Control: max-age=0
```

This causes repeated refreshes to keep paying the cost.

## Workaround

Putting nginx in front of WebUI and handling `/assets/` with gzip + proxy cache avoids the delay:

- nginx proxy URL: `http://127.0.0.1:8651`
- gzip response time for the same asset: ~35ms
- response headers:

```http
Content-Encoding: gzip
Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
```

However, this workaround requires careful WebSocket proxy configuration. The WebUI Socket.IO origin check compares `Origin` with `Host`; if nginx forwards `Host: 127.0.0.1:8648` while the browser origin is `http://127.0.0.1:8651`, WebSocket is rejected as `origin not allowed`. Passing through the original Host (`proxy_set_header Host $http_host`) fixes the proxy case.

## Why this matters

This makes the WebUI feel slow even on localhost and can look like a server/network problem in DevTools, because the time is reported as `Waiting for server response`. It is especially noticeable for Mermaid/Monaco bundles.

## Suggested fix

- Generate and serve precompressed static assets, or disable on-the-fly Brotli for large static JS.
- Add immutable long-term cache headers for content-hashed `/assets/*` files.
- Optionally document the recommended production/local reverse proxy settings for static caching and WebSocket origin forwarding.

items.body:
## Summary

The seeded default `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` silently replaces `DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY` with the template's own editing instructions, so every fresh install runs with no real identity in slot #1.

## Details

`hermes_cli/config.py::_ensure_default_soul_md` seeds `DEFAULT_SOUL_MD` (a markdown heading plus an HTML comment explaining how to customize the persona) into `~/.hermes/SOUL.md` on first run.

`agent/prompt_builder.py::load_soul_md` only checks that the file content is non-empty after `strip()`. A heading + HTML comment is non-empty, so the pristine template is returned as persona content. In `agent/system_prompt.py::build_system_prompt_parts` that makes `_soul_loaded = True`, and the fallback `DEFAULT_AGENT_IDENTITY` ("You are Hermes Agent, an intelligent AI assistant created by Nous Research...") is never appended.

Net effect: the system prompt of a default install opens with:

```
# Hermes Agent Persona

<!--
This file defines the agent's personality and tone.
...
Delete the contents (or this file) to use the default personality.
-->
```

…and the agent never receives its actual default identity. The template's own instruction ("Delete the contents to use the default personality") is defeated by the as-shipped contents being non-empty.

## Related doc inconsistency

The template comment says "This file is loaded fresh each message -- no restart needed", but `build_system_prompt_parts` caches the stable tier for the lifetime of the AIAgent ("Hermes never re-renders parts of this string mid-session"). One of the two should be corrected.

## Suggested fix

In `load_soul_md()`, strip HTML comments before the emptiness check, or compare the content against `DEFAULT_SOUL_MD` and treat the pristine template as absent. Either makes the shipped default behave as documented.

Found while experimenting with persona-slot instructions on a real install; happy to send a PR if the comparison-against-template approach is acceptable.

items.title: [Bug]: TUI message gutter leaks 3-space indent into copied text on lines 2..N

labels.name: sweeper:cannot-reproduce
labels.description: Sweeper: could not reproduce on current main

items.body:
## Summary

In the TUI, selecting and copying a multi-line assistant message picks up the
3-column left gutter as leading whitespace on every line **except the first**.
The first line copies clean; lines 2..N each carry 3 leading spaces. This makes
it impossible to paste a reply (email draft, code, etc.) into another program
without hand-stripping the indent first.

## Reproduce

1. `hermes --tui` in a terminal that uses alt-screen mouse selection.
2. Ask for any multi-line reply, e.g. a short email draft.
3. Click-drag to select the whole assistant block.
4. Copy, paste into a plain editor.

Observed: every line below the first begins with 3 spaces.

```
Hi Kayla,
   Tuesday works well. I have accepted the invite for 11:30...
   I appreciate the flexibility given the family schedule...
   Thanks,
   Nick Kinney
```

Expected: no leading gutter indent on any line.

```
Hi Kayla,
Tuesday works well. I have accepted the invite for 11:30...
I appreciate the flexibility given the family schedule...
Thanks,
Nick Kinney
```

This is plain `U+0020`, not an exotic Unicode space — verified by inspecting the
render path (the char pool fills empty/padding cells with `' '` and
`extractRowText` reads `cell.char` directly; no substitution anywhere).

## Root cause

`ui-tui/src/components/messageLine.tsx` (around L229-237):

```tsx
<Box>
  <NoSelect flexShrink={0} fromLeftEdge width={gutterWidth}>
    <Text bold={msg.role === 'user'} color={prefix}>
      {glyph}{' '}
    </Text>
  </NoSelect>

  <Box width={transcriptBodyWidth(...)}>{content}</Box>
</Box>
```

The gutter is correctly wrapped in `<NoSelect fromLeftEdge>`, but that box is
only **one row tall** (its child is the single role glyph). `NoSelect` marks
"every row this box occupies" — and it occupies exactly row 0. The sibling
`content` box is multi-line. So the noSelect fence covers the gutter on the
first visual row only; on rows 2..N the gutter columns are unfenced empty cells
that get copied as spaces.

The `fromLeftEdge` doc comment in
`ui-tui/packages/hermes-ink/src/ink/components/NoSelect.tsx` describes this
exact failure ("without this, a multi-row drag picks up the container's leading
indent on rows below the prefix") — but the mechanism only protects the rows the
NoSelect box itself spans, and here that is just the prefix row.

## Suggested fix

Make the gutter exclusion zone span the full height of the row, so the empty
gutter columns on the wrapped/continuation lines are also fenced. Options:

1. Have the `<NoSelect fromLeftEdge>` box stretch to the height of its sibling
   (e.g. the gutter and content share a row container whose cross-axis stretches
   the gutter, so NoSelect marks all occupied rows), or
2. Mark the left `gutterWidth` columns noSelect for the full height of the
   message block rather than per-glyph.

The fix should cover the whole bug class — any place a single-row `NoSelect`
gutter sits beside multi-row content (assistant messages, the `Response`
separator at L218-227, and tool-trail indents) has the same latent leak.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.16.0 (2026.6.5)
- macOS, TUI (alt-screen selection)
